Task branch landing order: building -> verifying -> ready -> in_bundle -> landed; side states conflicted, gate_failed and abandoned. Every branch is a ledger row with 1 owner and a time limit before it exists. fleetd owns conflicted and gate_failed: it starts a resolver attempt or a fix attempt of the task branch, and each failed one adds 1 to repair_attempts of the branch; at max_attempts the branch goes to the needs-you list, and horch branch abandon is the other exit (A27, A34). A bundle has the states building, gating, passed, landed, failed and dropped, and each ref move is a compare-and-set on the tip that fleetd last saw (A27, A34).

Worktree order: reserved (with 1 worktree_add job) -> created -> active -> landing -> landed -> removed, or orphaned when the owner dies, then rescued; a rescue ref is written and read back before any removal; a retried attempt reuses the same worktree. Rescue refs have 2 classes: unique (kept until the operator restores or drops it) and superseded (expires after 30 days) (A27, A32).

A usage limit or provider outage is not a stall: no attempt is burned (outcome quota); the task restarts at once on a fallback persona of another provider, else waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused. Long work is a job (A23, A32, A33): each piece of work that can take more than 1 s runs as a jobs row outside the reconcile pass. 2 classes: a pure job (task_check, fast_gate, full_gate, trial_merge), whose verdict is used again, and an effect job (bundle_build, rebase, rescue, fetch, push, worktree_add, worktree_remove, worktree_list, docs_sync, conformance), whose result is never used again. Each run has a run number; runs that end abandoned are bounded (abandoned_run_limit 3), and horch job requeue resets the bound. A git command that reads or writes a working tree, or uses the network, is always a job.

A reconcile pass has 3 parts (A24, A32): read the facts with no transaction, 1 transaction that decides and writes rows, then the effects. Each effect has a row in an intended state first (an attempt in launching, a worktree in reserved, a queued job), is keyed by the id of its row and is safe to repeat. A pass has a work budget, a time budget below the 30 s hang limit and cursors in pass_cursors. A periodic git fetch job records each remote tip in remote_tips.

The task state machine has 12 states, each with 1 owner and 1 exit (A26, A34): pending, ready, leased, running, stalled, verifying, blocked_on_user, waiting_quota, done, failed, escalated, cancelled. The outcomes asked, quota and critical_open burn no attempt. A dependency is met when its task is done and its task branch is landed. In a judge pair the judged task stays in verifying until its judge task is done, and each fix round is a new attempt of each, counted in fix_rounds. Each task state that is not terminal has an exit to cancelled.

Each request kind has a class, operator or worker, and fleetd decides at the server (A35). An operator request carries the operator token; the worker kinds progress, result and ask go through the outbox of the attempt. A requests row with a request_id makes each command idempotent, and a refusal carries its reason (A24). A file that a worker writes is not trusted: limits, no links, the real path inside its own attempt folder (SR-6). A file is an immutable message, a snapshot or an append-only log.

Decisions, with the options that lost

21 decisions · all taken · each option kept so you can see what was weighed.

D1step 1 · understandfoundationtakenby stephigh confidence

Is fleetd a change to horch or a new system that replaces it?

Achosen

Brownfield: fleetd is a set of changes to horch (keep, change, add)

Pros
  • Reuses the ledger, procid, herdr client, adapters and arch tests
  • Each phase keeps the fleet usable
Cons
  • Old shapes such as the v7 schema constrain the new model
Risks
  • A preserved behavior is dropped by accident
Why

The design says the design is a set of changes to horch, not a rewrite (Where multi-herdr stands today, Keep, change, add), and fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary (Amendment D9).

B

Rewrite: a new control plane that replaces horch

Pros
  • A clean model with no legacy shapes
Cons
  • Loses the preserved behaviors and the adapters
Risks
  • Lost work and a stuck fleet during the switch
C

Greenfield beside horch: a separate daemon that horch calls

Pros
  • Independent release
Cons
  • 2 versions of CLI and daemon can differ
Risks
  • Breaks C1: 1 binary, 1 version
Would flip if
  • The operator decides to fork horch into a new product

recorded as assumption A1 Lifecycle is brownfield: horch runs in production today, and the design is a set of changes to horch, not a rewrite (de…

D2step 1 · understandfoundationtakenby userhigh confidence

Do the 178 existing OS-specific sites in production code move behind the new platform layer?

A

Only new fleetd code uses the platform layer; existing sites stay

Pros
  • Smallest change
  • Matches the design's scope for the layer
Cons
  • 2 styles of OS code live side by side
Risks
  • Windows gaps in old code (Unix sockets, unknown machine probe) stay hidden
B

Move the existing sites that fleetd calls behind the layer as each phase touches them

Pros
  • Fleetd paths become first-class on all 3 OSes
  • Work is spread over the phases
Cons
  • Each phase grows
Risks
  • A phase gate covers less than the code it changes
Cchosen

Move all 178 sites behind the layer in 1 dedicated phase

Pros
  • 1 consistent rule enforced by arch_scan everywhere
Cons
  • A large change with no failure it fixes directly
Risks
  • Delays the phases that stop daily stalls
Why

Recommendation: B. The design makes Windows first-class (D1) but keeps the migration of existing sites as a separate decision. Moving the sites that fleetd calls, as each phase touches them, closes the Windows gaps that matter to fleetd without a big-bang phase. Strongest argument against: it blurs each phase's fault-injection gate with refactoring work. Decided by the operator (D16): option C. All 178 production sites move behind the platform layer in 1 dedicated phase, Phase P, between Phase 0 and Phase 1 (design amendment A19; Migration plan, Phase P). Reason: 1 rule that arch_scan enforces on all production code, and each gap of an OS visible in 1 file. The move changes no behavior (PL-6), and the cfg sites in test code stay.

Would flip if
  • Windows is not used day to day
  • arch_scan can enforce the rule only on whole crates
  • A phase gate fails because of a moved site

recorded as assumption A11 All 178 existing OS-specific production sites move behind the platform layer in 1 dedicated phase, Phase P, between Pha…

D1step 2 · discoverboundarytakenby strategistmedium confidence

Where are the pivotal events that cut the fleetd timeline into phases?

Achosen

4 pivotal events (assumptions approved, plan committed, task done, idea tasks landed) and 5 phases: clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating.

Pros
  • Each pivotal event is a state change of the design: approval gate, plan commit, verifier verdict, landed roll-up
  • Matches the actor changes in N7
Cons
  • Planning is a short phase with 5 events
Risks
  • Decompose may split planning from clarifying although 1 sub-orchestrator does both
Why

Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommendation: A. The design names an approval gate, a plan commit, a verifier verdict and a landed roll-up as distinct facts. Strongest argument against A: clarifying and planning are 1 sub-orchestrator on 1 idea folder, so the cut between them may not be a context boundary.

B

2 pivotal events (assumptions approved, task done) and 3 phases: shaping, building, integrating.

Pros
  • Fewer, broader phases; the conservative reading
Cons
  • Hides the landing state machine inside building or integrating
  • Hides the plan commit, the moment a task can first exist
Risks
  • Landing and feature integration look like 1 context
C

5 pivotal events (add task done split from verification, so a separate verifying phase) and 6 phases.

Pros
  • Makes the verifier a visible phase, as the design stresses 'done is a fact on disk'
Cons
  • Verification interleaves with attempts (check failed loops back to an attempt), so the phase edge is not a before and after
Risks
  • Decompose cuts a verifier context that cannot decide alone
Would flip if
  • The operator treats planning as part of clarifying
  • The operator wants the verifier as its own phase

recorded as assumption A2 The idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1…

D2step 2 · discoverboundarytakenby strategistlow confidence

Where do daemon supervision and adapter conformance sit on the timeline?

A

At the end of the executing phase, because they act on running attempts and profiles.

Pros
  • Keeps 5 phases
  • Near the attempts they protect
Cons
  • They are not part of 1 idea's flow
Risks
  • Decompose reads them as part of task execution
Bchosen

In their own 'operating' phase outside the idea flow.

Pros
  • Shows that they run on a schedule for the whole fleet
Cons
  • A phase with no before and after on the idea timeline
Risks
  • A 6th phase that is not on the timeline confuses connect
Why

Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommendation: A, recorded as assumption A3. Strongest argument against A: these events have no idea or task in their data, so they belong to a fleet-wide context, which B shows more honestly. The orchestrator chose B, not the recommendation A. Reason: the reconcile loop supervises each phase (sub-orchestrators in clarifying, landing rows, questions), not only executing.

C

Off the board, as a missing hotspot only.

Pros
  • Smallest board
Cons
  • Drops 04 S10 (restart on new binary) and the conformance gate from the model
Risks
  • A preservation row has no owner
Would flip if
  • Decompose finds a separate daemon or platform context

recorded as assumption A3 Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outs…

D1step 3 · decomposeboundarytakenby strategistmedium confidence

Is the verifier a context of its own, or a module of task-execution?

Achosen

Module of task-execution: verification is an aggregate beside task and attempt.

Pros
  • 1 transaction for attempt end, verdict and task state
  • The skill tie-break says merge when the boundary is unsure
Cons
  • The judge rank language (CRITICAL, HIGH) sits beside lease language
Risks
  • task-execution grows large
Why

Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. Verification shares the task states and the transaction of task-execution. Strongest argument against: the design lists the Verifier as its own component with its own rules for each task kind, so its rules may change apart from dispatch.

B

Context of its own (verification) that task-execution calls after attempt-exited.

Pros
  • Matches the design component 'Verifier'
  • Keeps judge and review rules apart from dispatch
Cons
  • Every done needs a cross-context call and an event back
Risks
  • The reap and requeue rule 04 S7 spans 2 contexts
C

Merge verification into integration, since both run gates.

Pros
  • All gates in 1 place
Cons
  • Mixes task done with branch landed, which the design keeps apart (understand N4)
Risks
  • The word done changes meaning inside 1 model
Would flip if
  • The judge and review rules change on a different schedule from dispatch
  • Verification must run outside fleetd

D2step 3 · decomposeownershiptakenby strategistmedium confidence

Which context owns worker questions: ideas or task-execution?

Achosen

ideas owns the question aggregate.

Pros
  • The sub-orchestrator answers against the idea's assumptions
  • revise-requested goes to the operator approval flow of the idea
Cons
  • The worker, an actor of task-execution, asks it
Risks
  • The attempt pause and resume crosses 2 contexts
Why

Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. The answer is an assumption of the idea. Strongest argument against: the attempt pause and resume then depends on another context. Source: design, the owner of a worker question is the sub-orchestrator of its feature (RR-12).

B

task-execution owns the question aggregate.

Pros
  • The attempt waits on it, so pause and resume stay inside 1 context
Cons
  • Answers create assumptions that belong to the idea
Risks
  • Assumption language leaks into task-execution
C

A context of its own (operator attention) for questions, approvals and escalations.

Pros
  • Matches cap-operator-attention
Cons
  • A seventh context above the 2 to 6 band at 1 deployable
Risks
  • A thin context with no own language
Would flip if
  • Answers never change the idea's assumptions
  • The operator wants 1 inbox context

recorded as assumption A3 The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator ans…

D3step 3 · decomposeboundarytakenby strategistmedium confidence

Are worker profiles and adapters a context of their own, or a part of task-execution?

Achosen

Own context worker-profiles.

Pros
  • Rate of change of the CLIs
  • 1 owner for the credential and environment rules
Cons
  • Only 2 events in the storm
Risks
  • A thin context until docs sync is stormed
Why

Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. The CLI adapters change weekly and carry the absolute credential rule. Strongest argument against: the storm shows only 2 events, and the skill tie-break says merge when unsure. Reason of the orchestrator: the environment scrub has 1 owner.

B

Module of task-execution.

Pros
  • Fewer contexts
  • launch-attempt already lives there
Cons
  • CLI churn changes the dispatch model
Risks
  • The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rule has no clear owner
C

Part of fleet-runtime, as a platform concern.

Pros
  • Sandbox is a platform service
Cons
  • Profiles are domain choices, not OS facilities
Risks
  • fleet-runtime mixes OS and CLI churn
Would flip if

The domain, as a tree

6 contexts. Open a context for what it promises; open an aggregate for the rules it protects. Every name links to where it is used.

Ideas ideassupporting · 1 aggregate · 13 ports

Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (worker-profiles). It owns the 1 needs-you list, where everything that waits for the operator is shown.

supportingdomain-modelteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/ideas

Kind of context
specification-modelapprover It builds a document, the plan, that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3) and then executed by task-execution: a specification model. It holds the operator approval gate, where an idea goes on only with the operator's approved hash (FR-10, I7): an approver. Decision D2 took option A (orchestrator, D15; [define A18]).

Rules it decides

  • Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).
  • An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).
  • The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.
  • While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.
  • When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).
  • A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).
  • Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).
  • A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded. After 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, the question escalates to the needs-you list, and the wait for the operator has no limit (RR-12, [define A29]).
  • The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, so fleetd stays the only ledger writer.
  • When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.
  • When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).
  • Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles start-agent-process (connect N3, [define A30]).
  • There is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. Approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks (task-escalated from task-execution) wait there for the operator; no other context shows the operator an item to decide (design OR-3, [define A25]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G3): count of tasks that exist outside a committed, validated plan, plus count of processes that planned 2 ideas at once. Target 0.
  • Business (G3): count of ideas past awaiting_approval whose approved_sha256 does not match the current assumptions.md (I7). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of ledger writes to ideas, plans or questions tables that come from code outside the ideas module (organise N2). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of items shown to the operator for a decision from outside the needs-you list of ideas ([define A25]). Target 0.

Task execution task-executioncore · 2 aggregates · 14 ports

Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles).

coredomain-modelteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/task_execution

Kind of context
execution-context It owns the task, attempt and verification aggregates and moves them through state machines with real invariants (I1, I2, I4, I5, RR-2, RR-3). Policies and the clock drive almost all of its 17 commands; the worker, agent CLI and provider pool inputs pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]), not a gateway role.

Rules it decides

  • Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4).
  • When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks.
  • fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5).
  • A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1). The herdr agent status (agent-status-changed) is 1 liveness signal; it never sets a state by itself ([define A23]).
  • Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4).
  • Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.
  • A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8).
  • A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11).
  • fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1).
  • Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then task-escalated puts it on the needs-you list of ideas (RR-6, [define A25]).
  • An operator requeue of a held task sets its attempt count to 0 (attempt_floor, 04 L8); a requeue by a review keeps its own counter ([define A28]). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration).
  • No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6).
  • A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5).
  • A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model.
  • When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12).
  • A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker. Task branches rebase at landing: a rebase of the feature branch does not wait for running attempts, and an attempt on an old base meets its conflict at landing ([define A27]).
  • No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5).
  • Every launch calls worker-profiles start-agent-process, which resolves the launch environment and starts the process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N8, [define A30]). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4).
  • task-execution and integration are a partnership: task-done, task-escalated, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened change together as versioned in-memory events, and a change of 1 state machine is planned with the other (connect N6, [define A24]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G1): minutes from a worker going idle on a held task until fleetd retries or escalates it. Target under 10 min (about 7 min by design).
  • Business (G1): count of tasks left assigned with an expired lease, from check_invariants I1. Target 0.
  • Business (G4): attempts burned by a usage limit or a provider outage. Target 0.
  • Structural: count of code paths outside the verification module that set a task to done (notes N1). Target 0.

Worktree custody worktree-custodysupporting · 9 ports

Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).

supportingactive-recordteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/worktree_custody

Kind of context
execution-context It owns the worktree aggregate, whose lifecycle (reserved, created, landing, landed, orphaned, removed) protects invariant I6 and rescue rule RR-9. The clock and policies drive its 4 commands; no person commands it.

No aggregates recorded (active-record); decompose named worktree.

Owns commands
create-worktreereconcile-worktreesrescue-worktreeremove-worktreedrop-rescue-ref
Owns events
worktree-createdworktree-orphanedworktree-rescuedrescue-failedworktree-removedrescue-ref-dropped

Rules it decides

  • A worktree row is written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees (FR-11). A row left in reserved by a crash is created or dropped on the next pass.
  • No worktree is removed until its commits, its uncommitted files and its untracked files are saved on a rescue ref under refs/horch/rescue/, and that ref is read back and shown to hold them (RR-9). A rescue that fails verification leaves the tree in place and escalates the task.
  • Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6).
  • Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6).
  • Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9).
  • A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6).
  • An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction.
  • worktree-custody is the only caller of git worktree add, remove and list, and the only writer of rescue refs under refs/horch/rescue/. It runs no rebase, merge or branch delete; integration does ([define A26]).

Landing and integration integrationcore · 2 aggregates · 13 ports

Integration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for its pull request, so that each idea reaches the primary branch through its own feature (G3) and no landing overwrites other work (G2). It serves the operator, who merges 1 tested pull request per feature, and the sub-orchestrator, which gets conflicts as resolver tasks. It finds conflicts between features early by trial merges and keeps each feature branch rebased. It does not verify tasks (task-execution) and does not remove worktrees or write rescue refs (worktree-custody).

coredomain-modelteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/integration

execution-context It owns the task-branch and feature aggregates and the land lock, with state machines and the no-loss invariants I8 to I12. Only fleetd code and 2 operator commands act here; git and GitHub pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]).

  • I8: a feature is merged only when its changes are in the primary branch by content, also after a squash merge
  • I9: a feature branch moves only by fast-forward to a candidate that passed its gate
  • I10: before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists

  • A gate pass goes stale when either judged tip moves (04 F5)
  • A feature is stacked on at most 1 older feature

Rules it decides

  • A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2).
  • A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch.
  • On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator.
  • Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9).
  • A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5).
  • Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11).
  • A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]).
  • Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10); worktree-custody writes it ([define Q6]). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12).
  • When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7).
  • When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task. The rebase does not wait for the running attempts of the feature; their task branches rebase at landing ([define A27]).
  • When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature.
  • A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default.
  • A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9).
  • An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).
  • integration is the only caller of the git branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete. It runs no git worktree command and writes no rescue ref; worktree-custody does ([define A26]).
  • integration and task-execution are a partnership: their 4 messages change together as versioned in-memory events (connect N6, [define A24]).

Worker profiles and adapters worker-profilessupporting · 11 ports

Worker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox of each agent launch, so that every agent runs on the operator's subscription logins and never with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (C2). It serves ideas and task-execution, which ask it to start each agent process: it resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper and starts it through the platform layer. It keeps the adapters of every agent CLI correct by docs sync and conformance tests, and marks a profile unhealthy when its adapter fails. It does not choose which task runs (task-execution).

supportingactive-recordteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/worker_profiles

Kind of context
enforcer Every launch of every context passes through start-agent-process and its launch environment, which apply the environment scrub and the login rules (decompose N2, N8, connect N3). It ensures that other contexts carry out the operator's credential rule: an enforcer. It owns 1 aggregate, the worker profile, with few commands, and the fleet-run wrapper ([define A30]).

No aggregates recorded (active-record); decompose named worker-profile.

Rules it decides

  • ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the environment of every launch: attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, detached child, updater and probe. The roster rejects a teammate file that sets it (05 E-10, 06 S1, understand N16, decompose N2).
  • agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2).
  • A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6).
  • A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1).
  • When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy.
  • The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10).
  • A new agent CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week; a CLI with unreadable release dates is held back. Pane auto-update stays off for claude and codex (06 S7, S8, C10).
  • Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15).
  • Every agent process starts through start-agent-process: worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping) in its own process group or job object through the platform layer, and never inside a ledger transaction (connect N3, N4, [define A30]).
  • The fleet-run wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json of its attempt with atomic writes. fleetd reads heartbeat-written into task-execution as a file, idempotently (connect A7, RR-8).

Fleet runtime fleet-runtimesupporting · 9 ports

Fleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops silently and no work is lost on a restart (G1, G2). It provides every other context with the single ledger writer, the command channel and the herdr adapter. It decides when fleetd is hung or old and restarts it. It does not own the platform layer, which each context calls directly, and it does not start agent processes (worker-profiles). It does not decide the rows of other contexts' tables (organise N2) or any task, idea, worktree or branch state.

supportingactive-recordteam Operator and agent fleetships in horch binarycrates/horch-core/src/fleetd/fleet_runtime

Kind of context
gatewayexecution-context It wraps the OS service managers and herdr for the daemon, through the platform layer, and translates them for core code: a gateway. It also executes the daemon lifecycle (heartbeat, hang restart, binary restart, schema migration): an execution context with no domain aggregate.

No aggregates recorded (active-record); decompose named job.

Owns commands

Owns events
fleetd-hang-detectedhorch-version-installedfleetd-restartedjob-abandonedjob-requeued

Rules it decides

  • Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5).
  • fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5, 06 S14, [define A33]).
  • When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7).
  • Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4).
  • Production code of the workspace has no OS cfg outside the leaf crate crates/horch-platform. Every context, fleet-runtime too, calls its 1 interface, and an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value that the caller decides on (PL-2, PL-3, [define A32]). Phase P moves the 178 existing production sites with no change of behavior (D16, PL-6).
  • New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5).
  • Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8).
  • The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2).
  • No git call or process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). After a herdr restart, fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files (C14). Agent processes start through worker-profiles (connect N3).
  • Worker reports reach fleetd as files, not through the Unix-socket channel relay or report socket, so Windows loses no report (06 S11).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G1): seconds of awake time from a fleetd hang to its restart. Target under 60 s (30 s threshold plus a 30 s check interval).
  • Business (G2): tasks lost or duplicated across a fleetd restart on a new binary (RR-7, OR-6). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of processes other than fleetd that open the ledger for writing, and count of OS cfg sites in production code outside crates/horch-platform (RR-5, PL-2, arch_scan). Target 0.

Where the data lives

1 deployable (modular-monolith) · within the 1–1 target · 1 store worth a look.

horch binary horchits own store · 6 contexts · flagged

3 contexts write the one store of horch; keep them in separate schemas or tables so the boundary stays visible when the deployable is split.

modular-monolithits own storedeploys on its ownteam core-team

fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI, the daemon and the wrapper always have the same version and horch self-update restarts the daemon on the new binary (design: Amendments D9, FM-34; understand C1). All 13 relationships are in-process calls and events (connect N1), task-execution reaches worker-profiles and fleet-runtime with synchronous calls (connect F2, F4), and 1 team owns every context. No split reason is in the inputs. Released through horch self-update and the GitHub release assets (understand C7). The platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform, linked into this binary (A9). Docs sync is a horch subcommand of this binary (D2, A10). worker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper role (A3).

The words

A word that means two things is where the parts were cut. Worth two minutes.

3 words mean different things in different parts. That is normal and it is also a line somebody has to keep straight: Assumption, Lease, Feature.

Every term69
TermWhereMeans

Step by step, in plain words

Each step in four sentences: what it did, what it decided, what it guessed, and what hurts most if the guess is wrong.

1understanddone1 on the listWhy the system should exist and who it is for.
what
We wrote down why fleetd exists, who it serves, what counts as success and how big it may get.
decided
fleetd is a change to horch, not a new product. It ships inside the 1 horch binary, for 1 operator and 1 team. Success is 4 numbers: idle tasks caught in under 10 minutes, 0 lost work, 0 tasks outside an approved plan, 0 attempts burned by usage limits. All 178 old OS-specific code sites move behind the platform layer in 1 phase, Phase P, before Phase 1 (operator decision D16). After the systems review (A23 to A37), long work runs as jobs outside the control loop, only fleetd writes the ledger from Phase 5, and a worker never runs without its sandbox.
assumed
The design gives no number for using the subscription fully, so we used a proxy: no usage window resets with usage left while work is ready.
riskiest
If the proxy for full usage is wrong, later steps may build pacing toward the wrong target.

11 guesses · 7 open questions · 27 notes forward · 2 decisions

  "constraints": [
    {
      "id": "C1",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary: 1 deployable unit, so the CLI and the daemon always have the same version"
    },
    {
      "id": "C2",
      "kind": "organisational",
      "text": "Absolute operator rule: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is never used and is removed from every child process, pane command line, detached child, updater and probe; every claude run uses the subscription login. agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL. Each process that fleetd, the wrapper, a job, docs sync or the conformance suite starts goes through 1 launcher that applies the environment rule of the profile and always removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (SR-7, A29)"
    },
    {
      "id": "C3",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "macOS, Linux and Windows are first-class hosts. Production code of the workspace has no cfg(target_os), cfg(unix), cfg(windows) or cfg(target_family), and no cfg! of these, outside the platform layer; it calls 1 platform interface with 1 module per OS, and an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value"
    },
    {
      "id": "C4",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "From Phase 5, exactly 1 process writes the ledger (SQLite in WAL mode, ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3); in Phases 1 to 4 fleetd and the horch commands write it, each through the same transition() (A36). Exactly 1 fleetd runs for 1 ledger: it holds an exclusive file lock and each write transaction checks its generation number (A24). Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start, a backup is written first (3 kept), a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger"
    },
    {
      "id": "C5",
      "kind": "organisational",
      "text": "Only the operator approves an idea's assumptions, with a command run outside any fleet process; a model can never approve for the operator"
    },
    {
      "id": "C6",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "fleetd keeps the behaviors of the Preservation analysis, among them 04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10 and M5"
    },
    {
      "id": "C7",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "fleetd keeps the contract surface: exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3, the mail contract for interactive panes, the UNLANDED and UNREGISTERED reports, horch self-update and its release assets, ticket format C1 and project facts"
    },
    {
      "id": "C8",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "fleetd keeps today's fixed values: land lock 1 h with 5 tries, check timeout 20 min (max 24 h), git push 10 min and other git network calls 3 min, code-sweep at most 2 requeues and review rounds of 1 (light) and 3 (full). Each git network call runs as a job, and its fixed value is the time limit of the job (A23)"
    },
    {
      "id": "C9",
      "kind": "timeline",
      "text": "Migration runs in 9 phases (Phase 0, Phase P, then Phases 1 to 7) in order. Each phase is released to every user at once when its gate test passes; the tests are the only gate. Phase 0 keeps a list of expected failures, so a red test of Phase 0 does not block a gate. Each requirement and each failure mode becomes green in exactly 1 phase gate, and each gate needs only mechanisms of its own phase or an earlier one (A30)"
    },
    {
      "id": "C10",
      "kind": "contractual",
      "text": "Agent CLI vendors set the terms: each provider pool has a usage window and limits, Codex user hooks need trust, and a new CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week"
    },
    {
      "id": "C11",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line written by fleetd's code; all hand-off between agents is through files written atomically"
    },
    {
      "id": "C12",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "Each agent works inside a context limit of 256k tokens"
    },
    {
      "id": "C13",
      "kind": "budget",
      "text": "There is no spend budget and no cap on features, sub-orchestrators or workers. Only health guards pause new dispatch: free disk, machine load, free memory, the count of processes and the count of open files of the user (OR-5, A28)"
    },
    {
      "id": "C14",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "herdr holds no state that fleetd depends on; after a herdr restart fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files"
    },
    {
      "id": "C15",
      "kind": "technical",
      "text": "A worker never runs without its sandbox: profile validation refuses a profile on an OS where the platform module returns not supported for its sandbox (preservation row 06 S9, A37). The sandbox of each worker denies a read of the operator token, a connection to the command channel and a write into the request folder, and fleetd refuses an operator request without a valid operator token (SR-8, A35)"
    }
  ],

2discoverdone12 on the listEverything that happens in the business, named.
what
This step lists, in time order, everything that happens to 1 idea in fleetd: from 'horch idea add' to the feature merged in the primary branch, with the people and programs that cause each step.
decided
The idea flow has 5 phases cut at 4 moments: the operator approves the assumptions, the plan commits, the verifier marks a task done, and the task branch of every task of the idea lands on its feature branch. Daemon supervision and adapter checks are a 6th phase outside the idea flow.
assumed
An idea with no --to gets its feature row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. A worker question waits 15 min for its sub-orchestrator before it goes to the operator.
riskiest
The words 'ready' and 'landed' each name 2 or 3 states. The design now makes each message name the entity with the state. If a later step drops the entity, a status can say work is safe when it has not reached the primary branch.

      "id": "sub-orchestrator",
      "name": "Sub-orchestrator",
      "from_understand": "sub-orchestrator"
    },
    {
      "id": "worker",
      "name": "Worker",
      "from_understand": "worker"
    },
    {
      "id": "friend",
      "name": "Friend",
      "from_understand": "friend"
    }
  ],
  "external_systems": [
    {
      "id": "clock",
      "name": "Clock",
      "description": "The fleetd reconcile pass (every 5 s) and the fixed timers it reads. It fires every time-triggered command. Each operational timer is a deadline on the fleet clock, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down (A25)."
    },
    {
      "id": "agent-cli",
      "name": "Agent CLI process",
      "description": "The Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, pi or Prime process of 1 attempt. Its exit is a process fact that the wrapper and the platform layer report."
    },
    {
      "id": "git",
      "name": "git",
      "description": "Worktrees, branches, refs and merge-tree trial merges. The source of truth for 'in the primary branch by content'."
    },
    {
      "id": "github",
      "name": "GitHub",
      "description": "Hosts the pull request of a feature (pr setting gh) or the compare URL (pr setting manual)."
    },
    {
      "id": "os-service-manager",
      "name": "OS service manager",
      "description": "launchd, systemd, or a Windows service and Task Scheduler. Keeps fleetd and herdr running and restarts them."
    },
    {
      "id": "provider-pool",
      "name": "Provider pool",
      "description": "A usage pool of 1 provider (understand actor provider-pool). It reports usage limits, outages and window resets."
    },
    {
      "id": "herdr",
      "name": "herdr",
      "description": "The pane runtime in session 'fleet'. Shows panes, agent status and notifications. Holds no state that fleetd depends on."
    }
  ],
  "phases": [
    {
      "id": "clarifying",
      "name": "Clarifying an idea",
      "order": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "planning",
      "name": "Planning",
      "order": 2
    },
    {
      "id": "executing",
      "name": "Executing and verifying tasks",
      "order": 3
    },
    {
      "id": "landing",
      "name": "Landing task branches",
      "order": 4
    },
    {
      "id": "integrating",
      "name": "Integrating the feature",
      "order": 5
    },
    {
      "id": "operating",
      "name": "Operating the fleet (outside the idea flow)",
      "order": 6
    }
  ],
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "idea-captured",
      "name": "Idea Captured",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 10,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "add-idea",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "text",
        "featureId"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea add writes 1 immutable idea file and 1 ledger row in state captured. --to joins an open feature. With no --to, the idea gets a new features row at capture (orchestrator, D15)."
    },
    {
      "id": "sub-orchestrator-started",
      "name": "Sub-Orchestrator Started",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 20,
      "actor": null,
      "triggered_by": "start-sub-orchestrator",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "featureId",
        "pane",
        "phase"
      ],
      "description": "fleetd opens pane idea-NNNN with a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the phase. The idea moves to clarifying."
    },
    {
      "id": "interview-question-asked",
      "name": "Interview Question Asked",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 30,
      "actor": "sub-orchestrator",
      "triggered_by": "ask-operator",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "question"
      ],
      "description": "The sub-orchestrator asks the operator 1 question in its pane, after it reads the code and docs the idea touches."
    },
    {
      "id": "interview-answer-recorded",
      "name": "Interview Answer Recorded",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 40,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "answer-interview-question",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "question",
        "answer"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea note appends the question and the answer to interview.md."
    },
    {
      "id": "idea-amended",
      "name": "Idea Amended",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 50,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "amend-idea",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "amendment"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea amend adds 1 amendment file. Before approval it joins the interview. After approval it becomes a revise."
    },
    {
      "id": "assumptions-written",
      "name": "Assumptions Written",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 60,
      "actor": "sub-orchestrator",
      "triggered_by": "write-assumptions",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "assumptions[]"
      ],
      "description": "assumptions.md validates with no item marked [open]."
    },
    {
      "id": "feature-opened",
      "name": "Feature Opened",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 70,
      "actor": null,
      "triggered_by": "open-feature",

        "featureId",
        "name",
        "branch",
        "primaryBranch"
      ],
      "description": "fleetd checks the kebab-case name, then creates the feature branch. The features row exists since capture (orchestrator, D15). For a --direct idea with no --to it happens at acceptance."
    },
    {
      "id": "approval-requested",
      "name": "Approval Requested",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 80,
      "actor": null,
      "triggered_by": "request-approval",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [

        "assumptionsHash"
      ],
      "description": "The idea moves to awaiting_approval. fleetd posts a herdr notification and lists the idea under Needs you. The idea lease is paused."
    },
    {
      "id": "idea-parked",
      "name": "Idea Parked",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 90,
      "actor": null,
      "triggered_by": "park-idea",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "reason"
      ],
      "description": "The idea leaves the queue: 7 days with no answer, an escalation, or horch idea park. Worktrees are rescued first."
    },
    {
      "id": "idea-cancelled",
      "name": "Idea Cancelled",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 100,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "cancel-idea",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea cancel. Worktrees are rescued first."
    },
    {
      "id": "assumptions-revised",
      "name": "Assumptions Revised",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 110,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "revise-assumptions",
      "pivotal": false,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "text"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea revise sends the idea back to clarifying."
    },
    {
      "id": "assumptions-approved",
      "name": "Assumptions Approved",
      "phase": "clarifying",
      "sequence": 120,
      "actor": "operator",
      "triggered_by": "approve-assumptions",
      "pivotal": true,
      "data": [
        "ideaId",
        "assumptionsHash"
      ],
      "description": "horch idea approve, run outside any fleet attempt. fleetd writes approval.json with the hash of the assumptions the operator saw."

    {
      "id": "direct-idea-accepted",
      "name": "Direct Idea Accepted",
      "phase": "planning",
      "sequence": 130,

      "data": [

    {

  "policies": [
    {
      "id": "start-lead-on-capture",
      "name": "Whenever an idea is captured, start a sub-orchestrator for its feature",
      "when": "idea-captured",
      "then": [
        "start-sub-orchestrator"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "open-feature-on-assumptions",
      "name": "Whenever assumptions are written for an idea with no feature branch, open the feature",
      "when": "assumptions-written",
      "then": [
        "open-feature"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "request-approval-on-feature",
      "name": "Whenever the feature of an idea with valid assumptions is open, request approval",
      "when": "feature-opened",
      "then": [
        "request-approval"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "restart-lead-on-revise",
      "name": "Whenever assumptions are revised, start a fresh sub-orchestrator in clarifying",
      "when": "assumptions-revised",
      "then": [
        "start-sub-orchestrator"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "park-on-unanswered-approval",
      "name": "Whenever approval is requested and 7 days pass with no answer, park the idea",
      "when": "approval-requested",
      "then": [
        "park-idea"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "specify-on-approval",
      "name": "Whenever assumptions are approved, start a fresh sub-orchestrator in specifying",
      "when": "assumptions-approved",
      "then": [
        "start-sub-orchestrator"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "open-feature-on-direct",
      "name": "Whenever a direct idea with no --to is accepted, open a feature named from the ticket title",
      "when": "direct-idea-accepted",
      "then": [
        "open-feature"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "validate-on-plan-submitted",
      "name": "Whenever a plan is submitted, validate it",
      "when": "plan-submitted",
      "then": [
        "validate-plan"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "escalate-on-plan-refused",
      "name": "Whenever a direct plan is refused, escalate it to needs-you",
      "when": "plan-refused",
      "then": [
        "escalate-task"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "promote-on-plan-committed",
      "name": "Whenever a plan is committed, promote the tasks with no dependencies",
      "when": "plan-committed",
      "then": [
        "promote-task"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "dispatch-on-ready",
      "name": "Whenever a task is ready, dispatch it unless a health guard or pacing holds it",
      "when": "task-promoted",
      "then": [
        "dispatch-task"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "create-worktree-on-lease",
      "name": "Whenever a task is leased, create its worktree unless one exists",
      "when": "task-leased",
      "then": [
        "create-worktree"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "launch-on-worktree",
      "name": "Whenever a worktree is created for a leased task, launch the attempt",
      "when": "worktree-created",
      "then": [
        "launch-attempt"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "start-process-on-launch",
      "name": "Whenever an attempt is launched, write task.yaml and START.md, then start its agent process",
      "when": "attempt-launched",
      "then": [
        "assign-task",
        "start-work",
        "start-agent-process"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "end-on-stall",
      "name": "Whenever an attempt stalls, end the attempt",
      "when": "attempt-stalled",
      "then": [
        "end-attempt"
      ],
      "kind": "automatic"
    },
    {
      "id": "end-on-lease-expired",
      "name": "Whenever a lease expires, end the attempt",
      "when": "lease-expired",
      "then": [

  "read_models": [
    {
      "id": "idea-board",
      "name": "Idea board and assumptions (horch ideas, horch idea show)",
      "informs": "approve-assumptions",
      "used_by": "operator",
      "description": "Every idea, its state, what it waits on, and the assumptions to approve or revise."
    },
    {
      "id": "interview-record",
      "name": "Idea folder (idea.md, amendments, interview.md)",
      "informs": "write-assumptions",
      "used_by": "sub-orchestrator",
      "description": "The only memory of a fresh sub-orchestrator process."
    },
    {
      "id": "in-flight-diffs",
      "name": "Diffs of in-flight features",
      "informs": "submit-plan",
      "used_by": "sub-orchestrator",
      "description": "The files that in-flight features already changed, so a plan can propose to build on one."
    },
    {
      "id": "approved-assumptions-and-spec",
      "name": "Approved assumptions, spec and decision log",
      "informs": "answer-question",
      "used_by": "sub-orchestrator",
      "description": "What the sub-orchestrator cites when it answers a worker question."
    },
    {
      "id": "start-file",
      "name": "Task file and START.md",
      "informs": "write-result",
      "used_by": "worker",
      "description": "task.yaml and inbox/START.md: goal, acceptance, lease, rescue commit and earlier progress notes."
    },
    {
      "id": "judge-findings",
      "name": "Judge findings",
      "informs": "settle-high-finding",
      "used_by": "sub-orchestrator",
      "description": "The ranked misses of a judge verdict."
    },
    {
      "id": "needs-you-queue",
      "name": "Needs-you queue",
      "informs": "requeue-task",
      "used_by": "operator",
      "description": "needs-you/ with the reason, the screen excerpt or the rescue refs of each escalation."
    },
    {
      "id": "worktree-list",
      "name": "Worktree list (horch worktrees)",
      "informs": "abandon-task-branch",
      "used_by": "operator",
      "description": "Every tree with its state, task, owner, age, size and rescue refs."
    },
    {
      "id": "pull-request-view",
      "name": "Pull request or compare view",
      "informs": "merge-pull-request",
      "used_by": "operator",
      "description": "The feature diff over the primary branch with its full gate result."
    },
    {
      "id": "launch-environment",
      "name": "Launch environment of a profile",
      "informs": "start-agent-process",
      "used_by": null,
      "description": "worker-profiles resolves a profile to the exact launch of 1 process: CLI, flags, scrubbed environment, private config home and sandbox profile. fleetd code reads it; no actor sees it."
    },
    {
      "id": "trial-merge-result",
      "name": "Trial merge result",
      "informs": "stack-feature",
      "used_by": null,
      "description": "The answer of git merge-tree for 2 tips: clean, or the conflicting paths. fleetd code reads it before it stacks a feature; no actor sees it."
    }
  ],

  "pivotal_events": [
    "assumptions-approved",
    "plan-committed",
    "task-done",
    "idea-tasks-landed"
  ],
  "hotspots": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "attempt-launched",
      "text": "Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity). Readers of today's ledger and code will read 'task' where fleetd means 'attempt' (understand N1)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "feature-opened",
      "text": "'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?"
    },
    {
      "id": "H3",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "sub-orchestrator-started",
      "text": "'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H4",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "task-done",
      "text": "'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H5",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "judge-verdict-written",
      "text": "'Judgment kind' (research, design, docs, report, creative) and the kind 'judge' sound alike. A judgment task needs a paired judge task; a judge task needs no judge. A resolver task has a code kind. Mixing them breaks plan validation (understand N12)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H6",
      "kind": "conflict",
      "near": "task-branch-verified",
      "text": "'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed."
    },
    {
      "id": "H7",
      "kind": "unclear",
      "near": "idea-captured",
      "text": "The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it? Answered (orchestrator, D15): the idea gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions."
    },
    {
      "id": "H8",
      "kind": "risk",
      "near": "task-branch-landed",
      "text": "The Preservation analysis rows (04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10, M5, 05 E-10, 06 S1 to S15) are hard inputs. Each must have exactly 1 owner in the model; a row that falls between 2 owners is a behavior fleetd silently drops (understand N15)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H9",
      "kind": "unclear",
      "near": "task-leased",
      "text": "What number counts as 'full use' of the subscription usage that pacing aims for? Pacing holds dispatch per pool window, but the design gives no target (understand Q1)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H10",
      "kind": "unclear",
      "near": "question-escalated",
      "text": "A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours. Answered (orchestrator, D15): 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, as a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit."
    },
    {
      "id": "H11",
      "kind": "external",
      "near": "fast-gate-passed",
      "text": "Plan validation refuses a project that has not declared a fast gate and a full gate, and this repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10, understand Q8). Until one is declared, no plan of this repository can commit."
    },
    {
      "id": "H12",
      "kind": "unclear",
      "near": "task-requeued",
      "text": "A task gets max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then goes to the operator. A requeue resets attempt_floor (04 L8). Does a requeued task also get a new replan, and how does the 2-requeue limit of the review scripts count against attempts? Answered in part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0; a review requeue keeps its own counter. The replan stays open (Q3)."
    },
    {
      "id": "H13",
      "kind": "risk",
      "near": "lease-expired",
      "text": "Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake. Answered (design A25): each timer is a deadline on 1 fleet clock in the ledger, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down. The hang check of fleetd and max_minutes of the wrapper use awake time from the platform layer."
    },
    {
      "id": "H14",
      "kind": "missing",
      "near": "adapter-conformance-failed",
      "text": "Docs sync and adapter conformance are collapsed to 2 events here. The flow that turns a drift into a task (who owns it, how a profile becomes healthy again) is not stormed. Answered (design, Docs sync and adapter conformance): docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules as a docs_sync job, then a conformance job. worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, and a drift becomes an idea."
    },
    {
      "id": "H15",
      "kind": "external",
      "near": "pull-request-merged",
      "text": "A project setting says who merges a feature; the default is the operator. When the setting lets fleetd merge, which gate and which actor stands for the merge decision? Answered (design A28, the feature state table): the owner of a ready feature is the operator, or fleetd when the project sets the merge to automatic. The gate is the full gate on the feature tip over the fetched primary tip."
    }
  ],

  "glossary": [
    {
      "term": "Idea",
      "definition": "A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it.",
      "avoid": [
        "ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea)",
        "request"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Feature",
      "definition": "1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. The task kind 'feature' is a different thing (H2).",
      "avoid": [
        "project",
        "epic"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Sub-Orchestrator",
      "definition": "The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase.",
      "avoid": [
        "orchestrator",
        "lead"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Assumption",
      "definition": "1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; the sub-orchestrator can also record its own reversible one.",
      "avoid": [
        "requirement"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Plan",
      "definition": "The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan.",
      "avoid": [
        "ticket list"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Task",
      "definition": "A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1).",
      "avoid": [
        "job",
        "claim"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Attempt",
      "definition": "1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd.",
      "avoid": [
        "run",
        "session"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Lease",
      "definition": "The time-limited hold of an attempt on its task that renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota.",
      "avoid": [
        "claim",
        "lock"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Worktree",
      "definition": "The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued.",
      "avoid": [
        "checkout",
        "workspace"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Rescue Ref",
      "definition": "A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase.",
      "avoid": [
        "backup",
        "archive ref (a different ref family)"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Task Branch",
      "definition": "The branch of 1 task that lands on its feature branch through the landing state machine.",
      "avoid": [
        "worker branch"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Feature Branch",
      "definition": "The branch of 1 feature that collects its landed task branches and reaches the primary branch through 1 pull request.",
      "avoid": [
        "integration branch"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Primary Branch",
      "definition": "The base branch of a project; main in this repository, not in every project.",
      "avoid": [
        "main",
        "master",
        "trunk"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Bundle",
      "definition": "1 candidate made from the feature branch tip plus every ready task branch of that feature, tested once by the fast gate.",
      "avoid": [
        "batch",
        "merge train"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Fast Gate",
      "definition": "The declared unit-test command of a project that every bundle and every rebased feature branch must pass.",
      "avoid": [
        "CI",
        "check"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Full Gate",
      "definition": "The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests, run on a feature tip over the current primary branch; a pass goes stale when either tip moves.",
      "avoid": [
        "CI",
        "e2e run"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Trial Merge",
      "definition": "A merge-tree result between 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, recorded in the ledger with no checkout.",
      "avoid": [
        "dry run"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Resolver Task",
      "definition": "A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files.",
      "avoid": [
        "merge task"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Judge Task",
      "definition": "A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5).",
      "avoid": [
        "review task",
        "judgment task"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Fallback",
      "definition": "The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage.",
      "avoid": [
        "backup model"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Job",
      "definition": "A piece of work that can take more than 1 s, run in its own process outside the reconcile pass and recorded as a jobs row. A pure job has a verdict that is used again; an effect job runs again each time.",
      "avoid": [
        "background task",
        "async task"
      ],
      "context": null
    },
    {
      "term": "Fleet Clock",
      "definition": "The count of seconds in the fleetd row of the ledger that each pass advances by at most 2 pass periods. Every operational deadline uses it, so a sleep fires no deadline.",
      "avoid": [
        "wall clock",
        "awake time"
      ],
      "context": null
    }
  ]
}
3decomposedone18 on the listWhere the lines are drawn between the parts.
what
This step cut fleetd into 6 parts, each with its own words and its own data: ideas, task execution, worktree custody, landing and integration, worker profiles, and the fleet runtime.
decided
6 parts, all modules inside the 1 horch binary, joined by 13 named links. Each of the 83 events and 65 commands has exactly 1 owner. The platform layer is a shared library that every part calls, not a part.
assumed
The verifier lives inside task execution, and worker questions live inside ideas. The orchestrator chose both (D1, D2), and the operator can reverse them.
riskiest
If worker profiles is not its own part, the rule that strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from every launch has no single owner, and 1 missed launch path bills the API key.

11 guesses · 0 open questions · 15 notes forward · 4 decisions

Everything else this step recorded44 key(s), shown so a change to the chain cannot hide data
