  "relationships": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "upstream": "ideas",
      "downstream": "integration",
      "pattern": "published-language",
      "description": "ideas -> integration, published-language: assumptions-written and direct-idea-accepted (ideaId, featureId) trigger open-feature. Upstream is ideas because the idea events are its to change. Integration consumes them as-is and needs no change in ideas, so not customer-supplier. Async through the reconcile pass."
    },
    {
      "id": "R2",
      "upstream": "ideas",
      "downstream": "task-execution",
      "pattern": "customer-supplier",
      "description": "ideas -> task-execution, customer-supplier: plan-committed and task-replanned trigger promote-task; plan-refused triggers escalate-task; question-answered and own-assumption-recorded trigger launch-attempt. The committed plan.yaml is the contract that every task comes from, and plan validation exists to serve task-execution (checks, owner paths, paired judges), so task-execution's needs shape ideas' plan schema. Async. From A34: idea-cancelled triggers cancel-task for each task of the idea that is not terminal."
    },
    {
      "id": "R3",
      "upstream": "task-execution",
      "downstream": "ideas",
      "pattern": "published-language",
      "description": "task-execution -> ideas, published-language: replan-requested (taskId, attempts) triggers replan-task by the sub-orchestrator after the last attempt. ideas consumes the event as-is. Separate from R2 because the direction of influence is reversed for this fact. Async."
    },
    {
      "id": "R4",
      "upstream": "task-execution",
      "downstream": "worktree-custody",
      "pattern": "customer-supplier",
      "description": "task-execution -> worktree-custody, customer-supplier: task-leased triggers create-worktree; the worktree lease row is written in the same transaction as the task lease. worktree-custody serves the dispatch need (1 worktree per task before launch). The pair also carries the attempt end: active to created or orphaned. Sync inside the fleetd pass."
    },
    {
      "id": "R5",
      "upstream": "worktree-custody",
      "downstream": "task-execution",
      "pattern": "published-language",
      "description": "worktree-custody -> task-execution, published-language: worktree-created triggers launch-attempt; rescue-failed triggers escalate-task. task-execution reacts to worktree facts as-is. Async through the reconcile pass."
    },
    {
      "id": "R6",
      "upstream": "task-execution",
      "downstream": "integration",
      "pattern": "partnership",
      "description": "task-execution -> integration, partnership (orchestrator, D15): task-done triggers mark-branch-ready; task-escalated lets the operator run abandon-task-branch. Integration asks task-execution to run triage and resolver tasks (open-triage-task, open-resolver-task create normal tasks). R6 and R7 change together: the 2 contexts plan their changes together. Async. From A34: task-cancelled triggers abandon-task-branch after a rescue ref; attempt-failed of a resolver or fix attempt at max_attempts triggers escalate-task-branch."
    },
    {
      "id": "R7",
      "upstream": "integration",
      "downstream": "task-execution",
      "pattern": "partnership",
      "description": "integration -> task-execution, partnership (orchestrator, D15): task-branch-conflicted triggers launch-attempt on the same task. R6 and R7 change together: the 2 contexts plan their changes together. Async. From A27: task-branch-gate-failed starts a fix attempt of the task; task-branch-repair-escalated lets the operator run requeue-task."
    },
    {
      "id": "R8",
      "upstream": "integration",
      "downstream": "worktree-custody",
      "pattern": "published-language",
      "description": "integration -> worktree-custody, published-language: task-branch-landed triggers remove-worktree; the worktree moves to landing and landed with its task branch (N6). worktree-custody still refuses a removal that would lose work (04 W6). Async."
    },
    {
      "id": "R9",
      "upstream": "integration",

4strategizedone3 on the listWhich parts are worth our best effort, and which to buy.
what
We decided which parts of fleetd need the most careful design, and which parts stay simple.
decided
2 of 6 parts are core: running and checking tasks, and landing branches on features. The other 4 parts are built simply, except the plan checks of the ideas part, which get a careful model. The ledger rows are the truth, and the events table is an audit log. We buy nothing new. herdr and the OS service managers are used as they are. After the systems review, fleet-runtime does more infrastructure work (jobs, the fleet clock, the operator token), but it stays supporting.
assumed
The ideas part is not core, because an AI does its hard thinking and the code is 1 fixed state machine plus the plan checks.
riskiest
If the simple parts of the ideas part (intake and questions) grow rules, the flat design there will leak bugs.

5connectstale15 on the listHow the parts talk to each other.
what
We drew how the 6 parts of fleetd pass work to each other, in 9 step-by-step flows and 51 named messages.
decided
All 6 parts run in 1 program, so they talk by in-memory messages that a 5-second loop re-checks. Only the operator's commands, the agents' files, herdr, git, GitHub and process starts leave the program. worker-profiles starts every agent process.
assumed
We assumed a lost in-memory message is harmless because the loop re-reads the database every 5 seconds and redoes missing work.
riskiest
If a part reacts twice to the same message and is not built to ignore the repeat, it can launch a worker twice or open 2 features for 1 idea.

      "id": "add-idea",

      "producer": "operator",

      "contract": "ui",
      "payload": [
        "text",
        "feature_id?",
        "idempotency_key"

      "delivery": "sync",
      "response_payload": [
        "outcome (accepted or refused)",
        "reason (when refused)"
      ],
      "channels": [
        {
          "via": "file",
          "sync": false,
          "delivery": "at-least-once",
          "note": "request file under the state root when fleetd is down; fleetd reads it at start; the file carries the same idempotency_key"
        }
      ],
      "description": "horch idea add",
      "idempotency": "fleetd applies a request once per idempotency_key and returns the first outcome again"
    },

      "idempotency": "1 process per attempt_id, or per idea_id for a sub-orchestrator; a start for a live recorded process is a no-op"

    {

      "description": "task.yaml, written by fleetd from the committed plan (design: Workspace layout and file protocol)"

  "coupling_concerns": [
    {
      "id": "CC1",
      "text": "task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other.",

        "task-execution",
        "integration"
      ],

      "smell": "bidirectional",
      "flows": [
        "F3",
        "F6",
        "F7"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Keep both directions as versioned in-memory events only, never direct calls. The orchestrator (D15) declared R6 and R7 a partnership: the 2 contexts plan their changes together (answers Q4).",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC2",
      "text": "ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas.",
      "contexts": [
        "ideas",
        "task-execution"
      ],

      "smell": "bidirectional",
      "flows": [
        "F2",
        "F5",
        "F6"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Accepted: decompose split the 2 directions into R2 and R3 on purpose. Both directions stay events.",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC3",
      "text": "ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back.",
      "contexts": [
        "ideas",
        "integration"
      ],
      "severity": "medium",
      "smell": "bidirectional",
      "flows": [
        "F1",
        "F3",
        "F7"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Accepted: R1 and R9 are both published languages; ideas never reads git and integration never reads idea files.",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC4",
      "text": "task-execution and worktree-custody depend on each other (R4 and R5): the worktree lifecycle follows the task lease and the attempt end, and launch waits for the worktree.",
      "contexts": [
        "task-execution",
        "worktree-custody"
      ],
      "severity": "medium",
      "smell": "bidirectional",
      "flows": [
        "F2",
        "F5",
        "F6"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Accepted as the lifecycle link of decompose N6; keep it as events in both directions.",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC5",
      "text": "task-leased is an event, but task-execution cannot launch until the worktree exists, and a failed git worktree add must come back to task-execution. The event hides a command that needs a result.",
      "contexts": [
        "task-execution",
        "worktree-custody"
      ],
      "severity": "medium",
      "smell": "event-should-be-command",
      "flows": [
        "F8"
      ],
      "mitigation": "task-execution acts as the process manager of dispatch: lease and worktree lease row in 1 transaction, then create-worktree, then launch on worktree-created, with a timeout back to ready.",
      "saga_candidate": true
    },
    {
      "id": "CC6",
      "text": "Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer.",
      "contexts": [
        "integration",
        "worktree-custody",
        "worker-profiles"
      ],
      "severity": "high",
      "smell": "external-in-transaction",
      "flows": [
        "F7",
        "F8"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Commit, then call, then record the outcome as an event in the next pass; never call git or start a process while the ledger transaction is open.",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC7",
      "text": "abandon-task-branch drops a task branch in integration, but the rescue ref that keeps the work is made in worktree-custody (04 W6). Both must happen, in order, or work is lost.",
      "contexts": [
        "integration",
        "worktree-custody"
      ],
      "severity": "high",
      "smell": "distributed-transaction",
      "flows": [
        "F6"
      ],
      "mitigation": "integration asks worktree-custody to rescue first and drops the branch only on worktree-rescued; integration owns this process.",
      "saga_candidate": true
    },
    {
      "id": "CC8",
      "text": "plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons.",
      "contexts": [
        "ideas",
        "task-execution"
      ],
      "severity": "medium",
      "smell": "wrong-policy-host",
      "flows": [
        "F6"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Keep the policy in task-execution only for a replan of an existing task; a refused first plan stays in ideas. ideas owns the 1 needs-you list (orchestrator, D15), so task-escalated goes back to ideas (F6).",
      "saga_candidate": false
    },
    {
      "id": "CC9",
      "text": "task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.",
      "contexts": [
        "integration",
        "worktree-custody",
        "ideas"
      ],
      "severity": "low",
      "smell": "wide-fan-out",
      "flows": [
        "F3",
        "F7"
      ],
      "mitigation": "Keep 1 thin event (branch, task_id, feature_id, tip); each consumer reads its own rows.",
      "saga_candidate": false
    }
  ],
  "sagas": []
}
6organisestale7 on the listWho owns what, and how many things we ship.
what
We decided who owns each part of fleetd and how many separate programs ship.
decided
1 team (the operator and the AI agents) owns all 6 parts. All 6 parts ship in 1 program, the horch binary, as separate modules. The OS code sits in 1 library inside it (crates/horch-platform), and docs sync is a horch command inside it too.
assumed
Each part keeps its own database tables and folders inside that 1 program, and no part edits another part's tables.
riskiest
1 team owns 6 parts, 2 of them core. An arch_scan rule checks the module walls; if the rule is weak, the parts tangle and a later split costs much more.

11 guesses · 0 open questions · 5 notes forward · 2 decisions

7definestale32 on the listWhat each part promises, one page each.
what
This step wrote 1 page for each of the 6 parts of fleetd. Each page says what the part decides, who it talks to, its words, its rules and how to measure it. Round 2 applied the decisions of the review.
decided
Only the verifier says a task is done. Only fleetd writes the ledger. No worktree or branch is deleted before its work is saved. worker-profiles starts every agent and removes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. ideas owns the 1 list of things that wait for the operator. git is split: worktree-custody keeps worktrees and rescue refs, integration moves branches.
assumed
The orchestrator chose cost-reducer for the core parts and specification-model plus approver for ideas. The operator can reverse both. We guessed that fleet-runtime owns the hang restart on all 3 OSes (06 S14).
riskiest
The rescue ref that must exist before a branch rebase (I10) belongs to worktree-custody, but the rebase belongs to integration, and no message joins them yet (Q6). A wrong answer can lose the old tip of a branch.

      "ubiquitous_language": [
        {
          "term": "Idea",
          "definition": "A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it",
          "avoid": [
            "ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea)",
            "request"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Sub-Orchestrator",
          "definition": "The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase",
          "avoid": [
            "orchestrator",
            "lead"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Assumption",
          "definition": "1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11)",
          "avoid": [
            "requirement"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Plan",
          "definition": "The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan",
          "avoid": [
            "ticket list"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Spec",
          "definition": "spec.md and requirements.yaml of 1 idea. Every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. It is written only after approval, in the phase specifying (FR-10)."
        },
        {
          "term": "Question",
          "definition": "A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator"
        },
        {
          "term": "Orchestrator",
          "definition": "Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Needs-you list",
          "definition": "The 1 place for everything that waits for the operator (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/): approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15)"
        }
      ],
      "business_decisions": [
        "Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).",
        "An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).",
        "The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.",
        "While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.",
        "When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).",
        "A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).",
        "Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).",
        "A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded. After 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, the question escalates to the needs-you list, and the wait for the operator has no limit (RR-12, [define A29]).",
        "The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, so fleetd stays the only ledger writer.",
        "When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.",
        "When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).",
        "Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles start-agent-process (connect N3, [define A30]).",
        "There is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. Approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks (task-escalated from task-execution) wait there for the operator; no other context shows the operator an item to decide (design OR-3, [define A25])."
      ],
      "assumptions": [
        "[understand A3] horch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage. (confidence medium)",
        "[understand A7] The alternatives are inferred from the design and the research files: today's horch with 1 orchestrator conversation, agents run by hand, and hosted merge queues (GitHub merge queue, bors, Mergify). (confidence medium)",
        "[understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)",
        "[discover A2] The idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1, option A, decided by the orchestrator, D15). (confidence high)",
        "[discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow (decision D2, option B, decided by the orchestrator, D15). The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline. (confidence high)",
        "[discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high)",
        "[discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)",
        "[discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low)",
        "[discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)",
        "[decompose A2] The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)",
        "[decompose A3] The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Decision D2, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)",
        "[decompose A4] Worker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 3 of their events (discover H14, N10). Decision D3, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)",
        "[decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)",
        "[decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15): approvals, interview questions, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts it on the list. (confidence high)",
        "[decompose A11] worker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started: it starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment of the profile (discover N10). This keeps the environment scrub with 1 owner (decision D3). (confidence medium)",
        "[upstream] … 18 more upstream assumptions name this context - see the step JSON files",

      "context": "task-execution",
      "name": "Task execution",
      "purpose": "Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles).",

      "ubiquitous_language": [
        {
          "term": "Task",
          "definition": "A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1)",
          "avoid": [
            "job",
            "claim"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Attempt",
          "definition": "1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd",
          "avoid": [
            "run",
            "session"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Lease",
          "definition": "The time-limited hold of 1 attempt on its task. It renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota (discover N1)",
          "avoid": [
            "claim",
            "lock"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Fallback",
          "definition": "The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage",
          "avoid": [
            "backup model"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Judge Task",
          "definition": "A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5)",
          "avoid": [
            "review task",
            "judgment task"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Resolver Task",
          "definition": "A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files",
          "avoid": [
            "merge task"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Check",
          "definition": "The acceptance command of a task. The verifier runs it in the worktree, in the sandbox profile of the worker"
        },
        {
          "term": "Done",
          "definition": "A task state that only the verifier sets, from facts on disk. It does not mean landed or merged (understand N4)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Ready",
          "definition": "A task state: every dependency is done and the task waits for dispatch (discover N6)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Feature",
          "definition": "A code kind of a task (with quality, refactor and security). It is not the feature of the integration context (discover N2)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Verification",
          "definition": "The check of 1 attempt's result that decides done: result.json validates, the task check passes in the worker's sandbox, and the review (code kinds) or the paired judge (judgment kinds) passes. It is the only writer of done."
        }
      ],
      "business_decisions": [
        "Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4).",
        "When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks.",
        "fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5).",
        "A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1). The herdr agent status (agent-status-changed) is 1 liveness signal; it never sets a state by itself ([define A23]).",
        "Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4).",
        "Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.",
        "A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8).",
        "A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11).",
        "fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1).",
        "Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then task-escalated puts it on the needs-you list of ideas (RR-6, [define A25]).",
        "An operator requeue of a held task sets its attempt count to 0 (attempt_floor, 04 L8); a requeue by a review keeps its own counter ([define A28]). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration).",
        "No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6).",
        "A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5).",
        "A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model.",
        "When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12).",
        "A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker. Task branches rebase at landing: a rebase of the feature branch does not wait for running attempts, and an attempt on an old base meets its conflict at landing ([define A27]).",
        "No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5).",
        "Every launch calls worker-profiles start-agent-process, which resolves the launch environment and starts the process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N8, [define A30]). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4).",
        "task-execution and integration are a partnership: task-done, task-escalated, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened change together as versioned in-memory events, and a change of 1 state machine is planned with the other (connect N6, [define A24])."
      ],
      "assumptions": [
        "[understand A4] The design gives no number for full use of the subscription usage. G4 uses a proxy: no pool ends its window with usage left while a task is ready, and a usage limit burns 0 attempts. (confidence low)",
        "[understand A5] A judge, a resolver and a triage agent are workers that run a task of a given kind. They are not separate actors. (confidence medium)",
        "[understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)",
        "[discover A5] The judge, resolver and triage workers are the 'worker' actor running a task of a given kind (understand A5). (confidence medium)",
        "[discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed).         "[discover A7] 'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event. (confidence medium)",
        "[discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low)",
        "[discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)",

        "[discover Q3] Does an operator requeue also restore the single replan (H12)? Answered part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0, and a requeue by a review keeps its own counter.",

        "[discover H1 near attempt-launched - conflict] Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity).         "[discover H4 near task-done - conflict] 'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done).       "context": "worktree-custody",
      "name": "Worktree custody",
      "purpose": "Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).",

      "ubiquitous_language": [
        {
          "term": "Worktree",
          "definition": "The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued",
          "avoid": [
            "checkout",
            "workspace"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Rescue Ref",
          "definition": "A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase",
          "avoid": [
            "backup",
            "archive ref (a different ref family)"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Worktree Lease",
          "definition": "Same as Lease in this context: the worktree row that holds 1 worktree for 1 task and 1 owner. It is not the attempt lease of task-execution (decompose N4)."
        },
        {
          "term": "Orphan",
          "definition": "A worktree, on disk or in git worktree list, that the ledger does not own or whose owner attempt is dead. It is adopted or rescued, never deleted."
        },
        {
          "term": "Lease",
          "definition": "The worktree lease: the ledger row written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. It holds the worktree for 1 task until its work is landed or rescued"
        },

        "Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6).",
        "Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6).",
        "Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9).",
        "A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6).",
        "An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction.",

      "ubiquitous_language": [
        {
          "term": "Feature",
          "definition": "1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas (understand N2). The feature aggregate owns feature-opened to feature-merged (discover N2)",
          "avoid": [
            "project",
            "epic"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Feature Branch",
          "definition": "The branch of 1 feature that collects its landed task branches and reaches the primary branch through 1 pull request",
          "avoid": [
            "integration branch"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Task Branch",
          "definition": "The branch of 1 task that lands on its feature branch through the landing state machine",
          "avoid": [
            "worker branch"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Primary Branch",
          "definition": "The base branch of a project; main in this repository, not in every project",
          "avoid": [
            "main",
            "master",
            "trunk"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Bundle",
          "definition": "1 candidate made from the feature branch tip plus every ready task branch of that feature, tested once by the fast gate",
          "avoid": [
            "batch",
            "merge train"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Fast Gate",
          "definition": "The declared unit-test command of a project that every bundle and every rebased feature branch must pass",
          "avoid": [
            "CI",
            "check"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Full Gate",
          "definition": "The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests, run on a feature tip over the current primary branch; a pass goes stale when either tip moves",
          "avoid": [
            "CI",
            "e2e run"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Trial Merge",
          "definition": "A merge-tree result between 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, recorded in the ledger with no checkout",
          "avoid": [
            "dry run"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Resolver Task",
          "definition": "A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files",
          "avoid": [
            "merge task"
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "Ready",
          "definition": "A task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle. A feature is ready when its full gate passed and its pull request can open (discover N6)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Landed",
          "definition": "A task branch state: the branch is fast-forwarded onto its feature branch after the fast gate passed (understand N4)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Merged",
          "definition": "A feature fact read from git by content: the feature branch is in the primary branch (understand N4)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Trial merge result",
          "definition": "The answer of a git merge-tree trial merge between 2 features, or a feature and the primary branch: clean, or the conflicting paths. Coined in connect (assumption A6)"
        }
      ],
      "business_decisions": [
        "A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2).",
        "A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch.",
        "On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator.",
        "Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9).",
        "A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5).",
        "Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11).",
        "A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]).",
        "Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10); worktree-custody writes it ([define Q6]). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12).",
        "When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7).",
        "When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task. The rebase does not wait for the running attempts of the feature; their task branches rebase at landing ([define A27]).",
        "When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature.",
        "A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default.",
        "A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9).",
        "An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).",
        "integration is the only caller of the git branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete. It runs no git worktree command and writes no rescue ref; worktree-custody does ([define A26]).",

        {
          "term": "Worker Profile",
          "definition": "The teammate file of 1 persona: agent CLI, model, effort, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, network, liveness, retry and fallback. Profile is its short name."
        },
        {
          "term": "Adapter",
          "definition": "The code for 1 agent CLI that turns a worker profile into the exact flags, environment and files of a launch, and reads its quota and context."
        },
        {
          "term": "Persona",
          "definition": "A named worker profile that a plan task names. Every worker persona names a fallback persona on another provider when the roster has one."
        },
        {
          "term": "Conformance",
          "definition": "The test that launches 1 adapter and reads back its effective settings (sandbox, context limit, hooks, scrubbed environment). A pass makes the profile healthy."
        },
        {
          "term": "Profile",
          "definition": "A named worker profile: the CLI, model, effort, sandbox and permission rules that 1 attempt runs with"
        },
        {
          "term": "Healthy",
          "definition": "A profile whose adapter passed its last conformance test. Dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile"
        },
        {
          "term": "Launch environment",
          "definition": "The exact CLI, flags, scrubbed environment, config home files and sandbox profile that worker-profiles resolves for 1 process launch. Coined in connect (assumption A6)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Start agent process",
          "definition": "The worker-profiles call that starts the fleet-run wrapper of 1 attempt, or 1 sub-orchestrator pane, in its own process group through the platform layer. Coined in connect (assumption A6)"
        },
        {
          "term": "Fleet-run wrapper",
          "definition": "The horch process role that runs 1 attempt: it sets the private config home, scrubs the environment, maps adapter events and writes heartbeat.json and exit.json (connect A7)"
        }

      "business_decisions": [
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the environment of every launch: attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, detached child, updater and probe. The roster rejects a teammate file that sets it (05 E-10, 06 S1, understand N16, decompose N2).",
        "agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2).",
        "A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6).",
        "A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1).",
        "When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy.",
        "The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10).",
        "A new agent CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week; a CLI with unreadable release dates is held back. Pane auto-update stays off for claude and codex (06 S7, S8, C10).",
        "Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15).",
        "Every agent process starts through start-agent-process: worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping) in its own process group or job object through the platform layer, and never inside a ledger transaction (connect N3, N4, [define A30]).",
        "The fleet-run wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json of its attempt with atomic writes. fleetd reads heartbeat-written into task-execution as a file, idempotently (connect A7, RR-8)."
      ],

        "Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5).",
        "fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5, 06 S14, [define A33]).",
        "When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7).",
        "Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4).",
        "Production code of the workspace has no OS cfg outside the leaf crate crates/horch-platform.         "New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5).",
        "Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8).",
        "The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2).",

      "requirement": "A task reaches done only from the verifier, from facts on disk (RR-3).",

      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When a worker process is stopped with kill -STOP during an attempt, then the alarm fires within 1 lease (120 s after stall_after) and the task is retried or escalated."
    },
    {
      "context": "task-execution",
      "attribute": "recoverability",
      "requirement": "A restart of fleetd loses and duplicates no task (RR-7, 04 S7).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When fleetd is killed in the middle of a reap, then after restart the attempt is ended and the task requeued exactly once, and outcomes equal a clean run."
    },
    {
      "context": "task-execution",
      "attribute": "availability",
      "requirement": "A usage limit burns no attempt; the task moves to the fallback persona or waits in waiting_quota (RR-11).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When a worker's pool reports a usage limit, then its attempt count does not change and the task restarts on the fallback persona at once or waits until the pool resets."
    },
    {
      "context": "integration",
      "attribute": "integrity",
      "requirement": "No branch moves except by fast-forward to a gated candidate, and no branch is deleted unless landed, merged or rescued (I9, I10, I12).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When a bundle fails the fast gate after a rebase, then the feature branch stays at its old tip, the branch resets to its tip from before the land (04 F7), and a rescue ref of the old tip exists."
    },
    {
      "context": "integration",
      "attribute": "correctness",
      "requirement": "Landed and merged are read from git by content, also for a squash merge (I8).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When the operator squash-merges a feature's pull request, then on the next pass the feature becomes merged and its ideas close only after every worktree is removed."
    },
    {
      "context": "integration",
      "attribute": "availability",
      "requirement": "A stalled git network call never holds the land lock for longer than its bound (04 F11).",
      "priority": "medium",
      "scenario": "When a git push stalls on the network, then it ends at 10 min (other calls at 3 min), is not retried, and the land lock is free for the next bundle."
    },
    {
      "context": "worktree-custody",
      "attribute": "recoverability",
      "requirement": "No worktree is removed before its work is landed or on a verified rescue ref (RR-9, I6).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When a worker is killed with dirty and untracked files, then after cleanup the rescue ref holds every file, read back before removal."
    },
    {
      "context": "worker-profiles",
      "attribute": "confidentiality",
      "requirement": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY never reaches a child process (C2, 05 E-10, 06 S1).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When the operator's shell has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and fleetd launches an attempt, a sub-orchestrator pane, a probe or an updater, then no child environment holds the key."
    },
    {
      "context": "fleet-runtime",
      "attribute": "availability",
      "requirement": "A hung fleetd is restarted on all 3 OSes (PL-5).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When fleetd hangs on macOS, Linux or Windows, then the heartbeat check restarts it within 60 s of awake time and the next pass continues from the ledger."
    },
    {
      "context": "fleet-runtime",
      "attribute": "portability",
      "requirement": "Core fleetd code has no OS cfg; a missing OS equivalent returns not-supported (PL-2, PL-3).",
      "priority": "medium",
      "scenario": "When the Windows machine probe returns unknown, then dispatch reports it and neither pauses nor treats it as healthy."
    },
    {
      "context": "ideas",
      "attribute": "integrity",
      "requirement": "Only the operator approves an idea's assumptions (FR-10, I7, C5).",
      "priority": "high",
      "scenario": "When a sub-orchestrator writes approval.json or runs horch idea approve, then the idea stays in awaiting_approval and fleetd ignores the file."
    }

8codestale36 on the listHow each part is built inside.
what
This step turns the 6 parts of the fleetd design into a code plan for Rust: which folders, which types, which interfaces, which tests, and in which order to build them. It writes no code.
decided
All 6 parts live as modules under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/. The OS-specific code lives in its own small crate, crates/horch-platform, that every part calls. 3 parts get aggregates (rich objects that guard their own rules): Task and Verification in task-execution, Feature and TaskBranch in integration, and Plan in ideas. An attempt lives inside its task, so a crash can never end the attempt and forget the task. worker-profiles starts every agent process and owns the per-attempt wrapper. The build order is the 9 phases of the design, with Phase P (moving the OS code) right after Phase 0.
assumed
We assumed the existing modules stay where they are and get wrapped, not moved. We also assumed nothing else may mark a task done: only the verifier can create the value that does it. Integration asks worktree-custody for each rescue ref instead of writing it itself.
riskiest
Wrapping old modules means 2 code paths live side by side until each phase removes the old one. If a phase forgets to remove its old path, the old watchdog and the new fleetd can both act on 1 task. Phase P moves 178 OS-specific sites at once; its only safety net is that every test gives the same result before and after the move.

    {
      "context": "task-execution",
      "implementation_pattern": "domain-model",
      "deployable": "horch",
      "module_path": "crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/task_execution",
      "aggregates": [
        {
          "id": "task",
          "name": "Task",
          "root_entity": "Task",
          "entities": [
            "Attempt"
          ],
          "value_objects": [
            "TaskId",
            "TaskState",
            "TaskKind",
            "AttemptId",
            "AttemptOutcome",
            "Lease",
            "AwakeInstant",
            "StallRung",
            "Backoff",
            "AttemptBudget",
            "PathClaim",
            "ProfileRef",
            "ResultFile",
            "VerifiedVerdict"
          ],
          "invariants": [
            "I1: a leased or running task has exactly 1 unexpired lease and 1 live attempt",
            "I2: no task is ready while a dependency is not done",
            "Only a VerifiedVerdict from the verification module moves a task to done (RR-3, define N1)",
            "A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal (04 S7)",
            "A usage limit burns no attempt (RR-11)",
            "An operator requeue resets the attempt count through attempt_floor (04 L8)",
            "A task has at most max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then escalation (RR-6)"
          ],
          "commands": [
            "promote-task",
            "dispatch-task",
            "launch-attempt",
            "renew-lease",
            "apply-stall-ladder",
            "end-attempt",
            "write-result",
            "schedule-retry",
            "mark-task-done",
            "escalate-task",
            "requeue-task",
            "move-to-fallback"
          ],
          "events": [
            "task-promoted",
            "task-leased",
            "attempt-launched",
            "lease-renewed",
            "lease-expired",
            "attempt-stalled",
            "attempt-failed",
            "result-written",
            "retry-scheduled",
            "replan-requested",
            "task-done",
            "task-escalated",
            "task-requeued",
            "fallback-assigned",
            "quota-wait-started"
          ],
          "state_transitions": [
            "pending -> ready (promote-task, every dependency done)",
            "ready -> leased (dispatch-task, lease and worktree row in 1 transaction)",
            "leased -> running (launch-attempt, after worktree-created)",
            "running -> running (renew-lease, earned activity only)",
            "running -> stalled (renew-lease lease-expired, or apply-stall-ladder)",
            "running -> verifying (attempt exit with a result file; write-result alone never leaves verifying)",
            "running -> waiting_quota (move-to-fallback with no fallback on another provider)",
            "running -> leased (move-to-fallback onto a fallback persona; attempt count unchanged)",
            "running -> blocked_on_user (worker question; exec worker exits and the task parks)",
            "waiting_quota -> ready (promote-task on quota-window-reset)",
            "blocked_on_user -> leased (question-answered or own-assumption-recorded)",
            "stalled|verifying -> failed (end-attempt with a non-verified outcome)",
            "failed -> ready (schedule-retry while attempts remain)",
            "failed -> escalated (escalate-task after the replan, or rescue-failed)",
            "verifying -> done (mark-task-done with a VerifiedVerdict only)",
            "escalated -> ready (requeue-task by the operator, attempt_floor reset)",
            "any non-terminal -> cancelled (plan change)",
            "rejected: done from any state without a VerifiedVerdict",
            "rejected: ready while a dependency is not done",
            "rejected: leased for a worker that already runs an attempt (I4)"
          ],
          "canvas_path": "ddd/08-code/task-execution/aggregate-canvas-task.md"
        },
        {
          "id": "verification",
          "name": "Verification",
          "root_entity": "Verification",
          "entities": [
            "JudgeFinding"
          ],
          "value_objects": [
            "VerificationId",
            "CheckOutcome",
            "ReviewOutcome",
            "JudgedTree",
            "FindingRank",
            "FixRound",
            "VerifiedVerdict"
          ],
          "invariants": [
            "A verdict is verified only when result.json validates and the check passes in the worker sandbox",
            "A code kind is verified only after the review scripts pass (V-14 limits)",
            "A judgment kind is verified only with no open CRITICAL judge finding",
            "At most 2 critical fix rounds, then the task escalates",
            "A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW finding"
          ],
          "commands": [
            "run-check",
            "run-review",
            "write-judge-verdict",
            "open-critical-fix",
            "settle-high-finding"
          ],
          "events": [
            "check-passed",
            "check-failed",
            "review-passed",
            "review-failed",
            "judge-verdict-written",
            "critical-fix-opened",
            "high-finding-settled"
          ],
          "state_transitions": [
            "pending -> checking (run-check, result.json validates)",
            "checking -> check_failed (run-check, check-failed)",
            "checking -> reviewing (check-passed, code kind)",
            "checking -> awaiting_judge (check-passed, judgment kind)",
            "checking -> verified (check-passed, judge kind: structural check only)",
            "reviewing -> verified (review-passed)",
            "reviewing -> review_failed (review-failed)",
            "awaiting_judge -> verified (write-judge-verdict, no CRITICAL item)",
            "awaiting_judge -> critical_fix (open-critical-fix, round 1 or 2)",
            "critical_fix -> awaiting_judge (fix written, a fresh judge checks the earlier CRITICAL items only)",
            "critical_fix -> escalated (a CRITICAL item left after 2 rounds)",
            "rejected: verified from pending, checking without a passed check, or awaiting_judge with an open CRITICAL item"
          ],
          "canvas_path": "ddd/08-code/task-execution/aggregate-canvas-verification.md"
        }
      ],
      "domain_services": [
        {
          "name": "DispatchPlanner",
          "description": "Picks ready tasks for workers across Task instances: I4, path overlap (04 L6), exclusive tasks, health guards and pool pacing. Pure: takes snapshots and a Clock reading."
        },
        {
          "name": "StallLadder",
          "description": "Maps a liveness snapshot (process alive, heartbeat age, activity age, agent state) and an awake-time reading to the next rung: doorbell, doorbell, end."
        }
      ],
      "application_services": [
        {
          "name": "PromoteTask",
          "command": "promote-task",
          "description": "pending to ready when every dependency is done, or waiting_quota to ready when the pool resets."
        },
        {
          "name": "DispatchTask",
          "command": "dispatch-task",
          "description": "No cap. Only the health guards (free disk, load) and the pacing of the pool hold dispatch."
        },
        {
          "name": "LaunchAttempt",
          "command": "launch-attempt",
          "description": "Starts the wrapper and the CLI in its own process group. A resume after an answer also launches. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after the ledger transaction commits (connect N3, N4)."
        },
        {
          "name": "RenewLease",
          "command": "renew-lease",
          "description": "Every reconcile pass (5 s). Lease time counts only while the machine is awake."
        },
        {
          "name": "ApplyStallLadder",
          "command": "apply-stall-ladder",
          "description": "Every pass: doorbell, doorbell after 2 min, then end. stall_after default 5 min; start timeout 90 s."
        },
        {
          "name": "MoveToFallback",
          "command": "move-to-fallback",
          "description": "Fallback persona on another provider, else waiting_quota with the lease paused."
        },
        {
          "name": "WriteResult",
          "command": "write-result",
          "description": "horch result writes outbox/result.json. Records the result on the Attempt. It never moves the task to done (define N1)."
        },
        {
          "name": "RunCheck",
          "command": "run-check",
          "description": "The verifier, with today's check timeout (20 min, max 24 h)."
        },
        {
          "name": "RunReview",
          "command": "run-review",
          "description": "Today's review scripts, unchanged. Rounds: light 1, full 3."
        },
        {
          "name": "WriteJudgeVerdict",
          "command": "write-judge-verdict",
          "description": "The worker of a judge task writes its verdict file."
        },
        {
          "name": "OpenCriticalFix",
          "command": "open-critical-fix",
          "description": "At most 2 fix rounds."
        },
        {
          "name": "SettleHighFinding",
          "command": "settle-high-finding",
          "description": "Fix or dismiss with a written reason."
        },
        {
          "name": "EndAttempt",
          "command": "end-attempt",
          "description": "Stops the process group through the platform layer (Linux: SIGINT, 20 s, SIGKILL)."
        },
        {
          "name": "ScheduleRetry",
          "command": "schedule-retry",
          "description": "Reads max_attempts and backoff from the profile."
        },
        {
          "name": "EscalateTask",
          "command": "escalate-task",
          "description": "Publishes task-escalated with its reason. ideas puts the task on the 1 needs-you list (A14)."
        },
        {
          "name": "RequeueTask",
          "command": "requeue-task",
          "description": "Resets attempt_floor."
        },
        {
          "name": "MarkTaskDone",
          "command": "mark-task-done",
          "description": "The verifier writes verdict.json. Takes a VerifiedVerdict; only the verification module can construct one (D4)."
        }
      ],
      "ports": [
        {
          "name": "TaskExecutionCommands",
          "kind": "driving",

        {

        }

          "invariant": "idempotent: attempt-failed",

          "state_transitions": [

            "ready -> open (a tip moves; the full gate pass goes stale)",

            "open|ready -> abandoned (operator)",
            "rejected: ready without a current full gate pass",
            "rejected: merged read from the GitHub API alone",

            "RescueRef",

            "BranchOwner",
            "Bundle"

          "invariants": [

            "I11: every fleet branch in git has a branches row; one without is adopted as an orphan row, never deleted",
            "I12: a branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it",
            "A task branch is ready only when its task is done (verified)",

            "A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7)",
            "An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator and only after worktree-rescued (connect N4)"

          "commands": [

            "task-branch-landed",
            "task-branch-gate-failed",
            "triage-task-opened",
            "task-branch-abandoned"

          "state_transitions": [
            "building -> verifying (task enters verifying)",

9contractsstale13 on the listThe exact shape of every message that crosses a line.
what
This step wrote 30 contracts: the exact shape of each file or request that crosses a process line in fleetd. These are operator commands, files the sub-orchestrators, workers and the wrapper write, files fleetd writes for them, and facts from git, GitHub, herdr, the agent CLI, the provider and the clock. Each contract has a schema, a good example and bad examples it must reject.
decided
Every field name is snake_case, as in the design (D1, option B). Each operator command carries an idempotency_key and gets back accepted, or refused with a reason. result.json status is completed, blocked or failed. reset_at is optional.
assumed
The idempotency_key is an opaque string of 1 to 128 characters, because no source gives its format. verdict.json decision is done or ready, from the Verifier row of the design.
riskiest
heartbeat-written and task-escalated sit inside 1 deployable, so the checker warns about them. If the wrapper later runs in fleetd itself, heartbeat-written stops being a wire contract.

What each part promises

One card per part of the business. This is the page somebody builds from.

Ideas ideasIdeas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea w

Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (worker-profiles). It owns the 1 needs-you list, where everything that waits for the operator is shown.

supportingdomain-modelteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).
  • An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).
  • The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.
  • While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.
  • When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).
  • A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).
  • Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).
  • A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded. After 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, the question escalates to the needs-you list, and the wait for the operator has no limit (RR-12, [define A29]).
  • The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, so fleetd stays the only ledger writer.
  • When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.
  • When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).
  • Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles start-agent-process (connect N3, [define A30]).
  • There is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. Approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks (task-escalated from task-execution) wait there for the operator; no other context shows the operator an item to decide (design OR-3, [define A25]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G3): count of tasks that exist outside a committed, validated plan, plus count of processes that planned 2 ideas at once. Target 0.
  • Business (G3): count of ideas past awaiting_approval whose approved_sha256 does not match the current assumptions.md (I7). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of ledger writes to ideas, plans or questions tables that come from code outside the ideas module (organise N2). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of items shown to the operator for a decision from outside the needs-you list of ideas ([define A25]). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is

  • specification-model
  • approver

TermMeans here

Task execution task-executionTask execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides

Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles).

coredomain-modelteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4).
  • When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks.
  • fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5).
  • A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1). The herdr agent status (agent-status-changed) is 1 liveness signal; it never sets a state by itself ([define A23]).
  • Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4).
  • Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.
  • A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8).
  • A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11).
  • fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1).
  • Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then task-escalated puts it on the needs-you list of ideas (RR-6, [define A25]).
  • An operator requeue of a held task sets its attempt count to 0 (attempt_floor, 04 L8); a requeue by a review keeps its own counter ([define A28]). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration).
  • No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6).
  • A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5).
  • A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model.
  • When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12).
  • A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker. Task branches rebase at landing: a rebase of the feature branch does not wait for running attempts, and an attempt on an old base meets its conflict at landing ([define A27]).
  • No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5).
  • Every launch calls worker-profiles start-agent-process, which resolves the launch environment and starts the process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N8, [define A30]). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4).
  • task-execution and integration are a partnership: task-done, task-escalated, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened change together as versioned in-memory events, and a change of 1 state machine is planned with the other (connect N6, [define A24]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G1): minutes from a worker going idle on a held task until fleetd retries or escalates it. Target under 10 min (about 7 min by design).
  • Business (G1): count of tasks left assigned with an expired lease, from check_invariants I1. Target 0.
  • Business (G4): attempts burned by a usage limit or a provider outage. Target 0.
  • Structural: count of code paths outside the verification module that set a task to done (notes N1). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is
