Worktree custody worktree-custodyWorktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no wo

Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).

supportingactive-recordteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • A worktree row is written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees (FR-11). A row left in reserved by a crash is created or dropped on the next pass.
  • No worktree is removed until its commits, its uncommitted files and its untracked files are saved on a rescue ref under refs/horch/rescue/, and that ref is read back and shown to hold them (RR-9). A rescue that fails verification leaves the tree in place and escalates the task.
  • Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6).
  • Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6).
  • Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9).
  • A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6).
  • An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction.
  • worktree-custody is the only caller of git worktree add, remove and list, and the only writer of rescue refs under refs/horch/rescue/. It runs no rebase, merge or branch delete; integration does ([define A26]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G2): count of worktrees removed without being landed, merged or saved on a verified rescue ref. Target 0.
  • Business (G2): passes in which an orphan worktree stays unadopted and unrescued after 1 pass. Target 0.
  • Structural: count of git worktree add or remove calls outside the worktree-custody module, from arch_scan (FR-11). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is

  • execution-context

TermMeans here

Rescue RefA verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase
Worktree LeaseSame as Lease in this context: the worktree row that holds 1 worktree for 1 task and 1 owner. It is not the attempt lease of task-execution (decompose N4).
OrphanA worktree, on disk or in git worktree list, that the ledger does not own or whose owner attempt is dead. It is adopted or rescued, never deleted.
LeaseThe worktree lease: the ledger row written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. It holds the worktree for 1 task until its work is landed or rescued

Landing and integration integrationIntegration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for i

Integration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for its pull request, so that each idea reaches the primary branch through its own feature (G3) and no landing overwrites other work (G2). It serves the operator, who merges 1 tested pull request per feature, and the sub-orchestrator, which gets conflicts as resolver tasks. It finds conflicts between features early by trial merges and keeps each feature branch rebased. It does not verify tasks (task-execution) and does not remove worktrees or write rescue refs (worktree-custody).

coredomain-modelteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2).
  • A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch.
  • On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator.
  • Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9).
  • A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5).
  • Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11).
  • A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]).
  • Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10); worktree-custody writes it ([define Q6]). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12).
  • When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7).
  • When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task. The rebase does not wait for the running attempts of the feature; their task branches rebase at landing ([define A27]).
  • When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature.
  • A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default.
  • A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9).
  • An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).
  • integration is the only caller of the git branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete. It runs no git worktree command and writes no rescue ref; worktree-custody does ([define A26]).
  • integration and task-execution are a partnership: their 4 messages change together as versioned in-memory events (connect N6, [define A24]).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G2): count of branches deleted while not landed, merged or rescued, or named by a git stash entry (I12). Target 0.
  • Business (G3): count of features marked merged whose changes are not in the primary branch by content (I8). Target 0.
  • Business (G3): share of landed task branches that hit a conflict. Baseline 2.7% of 376 (research-03 F7); target at most the baseline.
  • Structural: count of feature branch or primary branch moves that are not a fast-forward to a gated candidate (I9). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is

Worker profiles and adapters worker-profilesWorker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox

Worker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox of each agent launch, so that every agent runs on the operator's subscription logins and never with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (C2). It serves ideas and task-execution, which ask it to start each agent process: it resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper and starts it through the platform layer. It keeps the adapters of every agent CLI correct by docs sync and conformance tests, and marks a profile unhealthy when its adapter fails. It does not choose which task runs (task-execution).

supportingactive-recordteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the environment of every launch: attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, detached child, updater and probe. The roster rejects a teammate file that sets it (05 E-10, 06 S1, understand N16, decompose N2).
  • agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2).
  • A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6).
  • A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1).
  • When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy.
  • The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10).
  • A new agent CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week; a CLI with unreadable release dates is held back. Pane auto-update stays off for claude and codex (06 S7, S8, C10).
  • Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15).
  • Every agent process starts through start-agent-process: worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping) in its own process group or job object through the platform layer, and never inside a ledger transaction (connect N3, N4, [define A30]).
  • The fleet-run wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json of its attempt with atomic writes. fleetd reads heartbeat-written into task-execution as a file, idempotently (connect A7, RR-8).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (C2): count of child processes, panes, probes or updaters started with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in their environment. Target 0.
  • Business (G1): count of attempts dispatched on an unhealthy profile. Target 0.
  • Structural: count of agent process starts that do not go through start-agent-process or do not take their environment from launch-environment (connect N3). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is

  • enforcer

Fleet runtime fleet-runtimeFleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops sile

Fleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops silently and no work is lost on a restart (G1, G2). It provides every other context with the single ledger writer, the command channel and the herdr adapter. It decides when fleetd is hung or old and restarts it. It does not own the platform layer, which each context calls directly, and it does not start agent processes (worker-profiles). It does not decide the rows of other contexts' tables (organise N2) or any task, idea, worktree or branch state.

supportingactive-recordteam: core-teamships in: horchin the domain tree

Rules it decides

  • Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5).
  • fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5, 06 S14, [define A33]).
  • When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7).
  • Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4).
  • Production code of the workspace has no OS cfg outside the leaf crate crates/horch-platform. Every context, fleet-runtime too, calls its 1 interface, and an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value that the caller decides on (PL-2, PL-3, [define A32]). Phase P moves the 178 existing production sites with no change of behavior (D16, PL-6).
  • New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5).
  • Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8).
  • The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2).
  • No git call or process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). After a herdr restart, fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files (C14). Agent processes start through worker-profiles (connect N3).
  • Worker reports reach fleetd as files, not through the Unix-socket channel relay or report socket, so Windows loses no report (06 S11).

How you know it is healthy

  • Business (G1): seconds of awake time from a fleetd hang to its restart. Target under 60 s (30 s threshold plus a 30 s check interval).
  • Business (G2): tasks lost or duplicated across a fleetd restart on a new binary (RR-7, OR-6). Target 0.
  • Structural: count of processes other than fleetd that open the ledger for writing, and count of OS cfg sites in production code outside crates/horch-platform (RR-5, PL-2, arch_scan). Target 0.

What kind of thing it is

  • gateway
  • execution-context

Comes in from

WhoRelationshipMessages
clockconformistcheck-fleetd
frienduser-interactionself-update
os-service-managerconformistrestart-fleetd

Its words

TermMeans here
fleetdThe supervised daemon role of the horch binary (horch fleetd): the only ledger writer, which runs the reconcile pass of all 6 contexts every 5 s (organise N1).
HeartbeatThe time of fleetd's last full pass, written after each pass. horch fleetd check reads it. It is not the wrapper heartbeat.json of an attempt.
Platform LayerThe leaf crate crates/horch-platform: 1 interface with 1 module per OS (mac.rs, linux.rs, windows.rs) for process facts, process group stop, service install and restart, hang detection, file watching, sandboxing, sleep and wake, the command channel transport and the machine probe (PL-2, A19). It is not a bounded context; each context calls it (decompose N7).
Command ChannelThe local transport on which CLI commands and agents send requests to fleetd. fleetd validates each request and writes the result to the ledger.
LedgerThe SQLite file ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3 in WAL mode: an event log plus derived tables. Only fleetd writes it; each context owns its own tables (understand N17, organise N2).
Checkhorch fleetd check: the heartbeat check that restarts fleetd when its last full pass is older than 30 s of awake time. It is not a task check

Every message, field by field

31 written contracts. Each field shows its type, whether it must be there, and the value from the checked example beside it.

Rules you can rely on

  • Each accepted request creates exactly 1 immutable idea.md and 1 ledger row in state captured, and the reply carries its new idea_id.
  • Only fleetd writes the ledger. When fleetd is down, horch writes a request file and fleetd reads it at start, so the reply arrives only on the sync channel.
  • fleetd applies a request once per idempotency_key and returns the first outcome again; the request file of the same command run carries the same key (orchestrator, D15).
  • A refused request returns outcome refused with its reason (orchestrator, D15).

Terms of use

Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. The horch CLI and fleetd ship in 1 binary, so the operator never meets a version skew, but a request file written by an older horch and read at start must still validate.

Rules you can rely on

  • fleetd records 1 answer per question_id; a second answer for the same question_id is refused with its reason.
  • A covered answer must carry a citation, and fleetd checks that the cited line exists.
  • A revise answer goes to the operator and pauses only the affected tasks; an own_decision answer is recorded as an assumption the operator can reverse.
  • The answer goes to the decision log of the feature and to every later task of the feature.
  • fleetd applies a request once per idempotency_key and returns the first outcome again; the request file of the same command run carries the same key (orchestrator, D15).
  • A refused request returns outcome refused with its reason (orchestrator, D15).

Terms of use

a result names its task and attempt with the design field names task and attempt{"task_id":"T-0007-02","attempt_id":"A1","status":"completed","summary":"Done.","commits":[]}

Rules you can rely on

  • 1 result per attempt: result.json is written atomically and never rewritten; fleetd ingests it once per (task, attempt).
  • The result is a claim, not a fact: a task is done only when result.json validates and the verifier's check passes in the worker sandbox (RR-3, SR-4).
  • acceptance_self_check is advisory; the verifier never trusts it.
  • A process that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write it; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result.
  • status is 1 of the closed list completed, blocked, failed (orchestrator, D15). The worker's status is a claim; only the verifier moves a task to done.

Terms of use

Rules you can rely on

  • 1 needs-you/ file per (idea_id, assumptions_hash), plus a herdr notification; a revised assumptions.md gets a new file.
  • Waiting is not a stall: 1 reminder an hour during working hours, and after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.

Terms of use

Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. The horch CLI and fleetd ship in 1 binary, so the operator never meets a version skew, but a request file written by an older horch and read at start must still validate.

Response Open Pull Request response

FieldTypeExampleMeans

Must be rejected1
Why it is wrongPayload
pr is an https URL{"pr":"pull/349"}

Rules you can rely on

  • 1 pull request per feature_id; integration reads features.pr first and does not open a second one.
  • A retry after a timeout reads features.pr and GitHub first, so it opens no second pull request.
  • Every git network call has a wall-clock bound (push 10 min) and never retries (04 F11).

Terms of use

GitHub owns the wire contract. The schema is our view at the github adapter of integration; a GitHub change lands in that adapter only. Additive changes only within version 1.x.

Rules you can rely on

  • The reconcile pass is level-triggered, so the reaction can run again: ideas writes 1 needs-you/ file per (task_id, reason) on its 1 needs-you list, and integration records it once per task_id.
  • Nothing is removed on escalation: the worktree and branch stay, and only the operator abandons the branch.
  • An operator requeue of the task resets its attempt count (attempt_floor, 04 L8).
  • Both consumers run in the same horch process (organise): this entry is kept for the idempotent: task-escalated test of code.json, not as a wire contract.

Terms of use

Additive changes only within version 1.x; a removed, renamed or retyped field is 2.0. The horch CLI and fleetd ship in 1 binary, so the operator never meets a version skew, but a request file written by an older horch and read at start must still validate.

N8 Task branch landing order: building -> verifying -> ready -> in_bundle -> landed; side states conflicted, gat…for discoverprocess

Task branch landing order: building -> verifying -> ready -> in_bundle -> landed; side states conflicted, gate_failed and abandoned. Every branch is a ledger row with 1 owner and a time limit before it exists. fleetd owns conflicted and gate_failed: it starts a resolver attempt or a fix attempt of the task branch, and each failed one adds 1 to repair_attempts of the branch; at max_attempts the branch goes to the needs-you list, and horch branch abandon is the other exit (A27, A34). A bundle has the states building, gating, passed, landed, failed and dropped, and each ref move is a compare-and-set on the tip that fleetd last saw (A27, A34).

N9 Worktree order: reserved (with 1 worktree_add job) -> created -> active -> landing -> landed -> removed, or o…for discoverprocess

Worktree order: reserved (with 1 worktree_add job) -> created -> active -> landing -> landed -> removed, or orphaned when the owner dies, then rescued; a rescue ref is written and read back before any removal; a retried attempt reuses the same worktree. Rescue refs have 2 classes: unique (kept until the operator restores or drops it) and superseded (expires after 30 days) (A27, A32).

N21 Long work is a job (A23, A32, A33): each piece of work that can take more than 1 s runs as a jobs row outside…for discoverfor decomposefor strategizeprocess

Long work is a job (A23, A32, A33): each piece of work that can take more than 1 s runs as a jobs row outside the reconcile pass. 2 classes: a pure job (task_check, fast_gate, full_gate, trial_merge), whose verdict is used again, and an effect job (bundle_build, rebase, rescue, fetch, push, worktree_add, worktree_remove, worktree_list, docs_sync, conformance), whose result is never used again. Each run has a run number; runs that end abandoned are bounded (abandoned_run_limit 3), and horch job requeue resets the bound. A git command that reads or writes a working tree, or uses the network, is always a job.

N22 A reconcile pass has 3 parts (A24, A32): read the facts with no transaction, 1 transaction that decides and w…for discoverfor decomposeprocess

A reconcile pass has 3 parts (A24, A32): read the facts with no transaction, 1 transaction that decides and writes rows, then the effects. Each effect has a row in an intended state first (an attempt in launching, a worktree in reserved, a queued job), is keyed by the id of its row and is safe to repeat. A pass has a work budget, a time budget below the 30 s hang limit and cursors in pass_cursors. A periodic git fetch job records each remote tip in remote_tips.

N23 The task state machine has 12 states, each with 1 owner and 1 exit (A26, A34): pending, ready, leased, runnin…for discoverfor decomposeprocess

The task state machine has 12 states, each with 1 owner and 1 exit (A26, A34): pending, ready, leased, running, stalled, verifying, blocked_on_user, waiting_quota, done, failed, escalated, cancelled. The outcomes asked, quota and critical_open burn no attempt. A dependency is met when its task is done and its task branch is landed. In a judge pair the judged task stays in verifying until its judge task is done, and each fix round is a new attempt of each, counted in fix_rounds. Each task state that is not terminal has an exit to cancelled.

The feature state machine has 4 states: open, ready, merged and abandoned (A28, A34). The pull request follows the state, horch feature abandon is the only way to abandon, a merge with ideas in flight moves those ideas to a new feature, and each feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator (I7). push_state and pr_state are facts on the feature row, and remote = none is allowed. The needs-you list has a life cycle: each item has a stable key and the state open, resolved or superseded.

system5record
name
fleetd: the horch fleet control plane
one_liner
A supervised daemon inside horch that takes rough ideas from the operator, runs AI coding agents on them, and keeps every task, worktree and branch accounted for until the work reaches the primary branch.
problem
The operator runs a fleet of AI coding agents with horch. Tasks get forgotten, workers do not find work or sit idle on it, finished work is never reported, the watchdog misses updates, stacked ideas merge in one orchestrator conversation, and dead workers leave orphaned worktrees. Each failure comes from a job that horch still leaves to an LLM.
why_now
Daily stalls and lost worktrees cost subscription usage and operator attention. horch already has the parts (recorded PIDs, a supervisor per worker, worktrees per task, finish steps), and a design review on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12 approved the design.
lifecycle
brownfield
business_model10record
customer_segments
The operator: a solo developer who runs a fleet of AI coding agents on 1 machine Friends who install horch and get new releases through horch self-update
value_propositions
No task stalls silently: every task ends verified done or escalated with a reason No paid-for work is lost: every worktree and branch is known and rescued before removal Rough ideas in, approved plans out: 1 idea at a time, nothing built before approval The subscription usage is used fully across agent CLIs and providers Parallel features reach the primary branch through 1 pull request each, with conflicts found early
channels
The horch CLI (horch idea add, horch ideas, horch status, horch idea approve) herdr panes, the herdr sidebar and herdr notifications The needs-you folder GitHub releases and horch self-update
customer_relationships
Self-service from the terminal An interview with the operator in the pane of each sub-orchestrator Quick approval of written assumptions by the operator
revenue_streams
None: horch is the operator's own tool; the return is operator throughput (assumed)
key_resources
The ledger (1 SQLite file, 1 writer) The files of the fleet workspace (ideas, tasks, attempts, rescue manifests) Git repositories, worktrees and rescue refs The worker profiles in teammates/ Subscription usage of each provider pool The host machine: disk, CPU and memory
key_activities
Dispatch ideas through a fixed state machine Plan 1 idea at a time with operator approval Bind tasks to workers and supervise attempts with leases Verify each task on disk Lease, reconcile and rescue worktrees Land task branches and integrate features Pace dispatch to each usage window Keep each agent CLI adapter conformant
key_partners
herdr (pane runtime) Agent CLI vendors: Anthropic (Claude Code), OpenAI (Codex CLI), Google (Antigravity), OpenCode, pi, Prime OS service managers: launchd, systemd, Windows services and Task Scheduler GitHub (releases, gh for pull requests)
cost_structure
Subscription usage of each provider pool Machine resources: disk for worktrees, CPU and memory for agent processes Operator attention for interviews, approvals and escalations

rationale
Recommendation: B. The design makes Windows first-class (D1) but keeps the migration of existing sites as a separate decision. Moving the sites that fleetd calls, as each phase touches them, closes the Windows gaps that matter to fleetd without a big-bang phase. Strongest argument against: it blurs each phase's fault-injection gate with refactoring work. Decided by the operator (D16): option C. All 178 production sites move behind the platform layer in 1 dedicated phase, Phase P, between Phase 0 and Phase 1 (design amendment A19; Migration plan, Phase P). Reason: 1 rule that arch_scan enforces on all production code, and each gap of an OS visible in 1 file. The move changes no behavior (PL-6), and the cfg sites in test code stay.
would_flip_if
Windows is not used day to day arch_scan can enforce the rule only on whole crates A phase gate fails because of a moved site

whatThis step lists, in time order, everything that happens to 1 idea in fleetd: from 'horch idea add' to the feature merged in the primary branch, with the people and programs that cause each step.
decidedThe idea flow has 5 phases cut at 4 moments: the operator approves the assumptions, the plan commits, the verifier marks a task done, and the task branch of every task of the idea lands on its feature branch. Daemon supervision and adapter checks are a 6th phase outside the idea flow.
assumedAn idea with no --to gets its feature row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. A worker question waits 15 min for its sub-orchestrator before it goes to the operator.
riskiestThe words 'ready' and 'landed' each name 2 or 3 states. The design now makes each message name the entity with the state. If a later step drops the entity, a status can say work is safe when it has not reached the primary branch.

The policy start-process-on-launch now issues assign-task (task.yaml) and start-work (START.md) before start-agent-process: fleetd writes both files after the commit of the attempt in launching and before the launch (design, Supervision, dispatch order). 'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4).

H6 'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is…conflict

'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed.

H13 Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wron…risk

Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake. Answered (design A25): each timer is a deadline on 1 fleet clock in the ledger, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down. The hang check of fleetd and max_minutes of the wrapper use awake time from the platform layer.

Answered (design, Docs sync and adapter conformance): docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules as a docs_sync job, then a conformance job. worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, and a drift becomes an idea.

whatWe decided which parts of fleetd need the most careful design, and which parts stay simple.
decided2 of 6 parts are core: running and checking tasks, and landing branches on features. The other 4 parts are built simply, except the plan checks of the ideas part, which get a careful model. The ledger rows are the truth, and the events table is an audit log. We buy nothing new. herdr and the OS service managers are used as they are. After the systems review, fleet-runtime does more infrastructure work (jobs, the fleet clock, the operator token), but it stays supporting.
assumedThe ideas part is not core, because an AI does its hard thinking and the code is 1 fixed state machine plus the plan checks.
riskiestIf the simple parts of the ideas part (intake and questions) grow rules, the flat design there will leak bugs.

rationale

Plan validation is a domain-model module (it holds the rules of coverage, the DAG, judge pairing, the model guide and the declared gates). Intake and questions stay active-record. Reason: these plan rules are real invariants, and they decide whether a task may start; a flat model lets them leak into callers. The split is a module boundary inside the ideas context, not a new subdomain, so decompose stays as it is. The step recommended A: Recommendation: A. The strongest argument against it is that plan validation and the approval hash are real invariants; ddd-code can still give the plan aggregate invariant tests inside a supporting context. The design does not settle the classification, so the operator decides.

Phase 2 fault-injection tests (kill -STOP a worker; alarm within 1 lease) and 0 tasks left assigned with an expired lease (G1 metric).

summarystring
2 of 6 subdomains are core: task-execution (decisive) and integration. Ideas, worktree-custody, worker-profiles and fleet-runtime are supporting and built simply; only the plan validation module of ideas gets a domain model (D1 option C). The ledger is a domain model with an audit events table, not event-sourced (D2 option A). Nothing is generic: herdr and the OS service managers are adopted inside fleet-runtime as adapters. Every subdomain is built in horch-core, and the platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform.

whatWe drew how the 6 parts of fleetd pass work to each other, in 9 step-by-step flows and 51 named messages.
decidedAll 6 parts run in 1 program, so they talk by in-memory messages that a 5-second loop re-checks. Only the operator's commands, the agents' files, herdr, git, GitHub and process starts leave the program. worker-profiles starts every agent process.
assumedWe assumed a lost in-memory message is harmless because the loop re-reads the database every 5 seconds and redoes missing work.
riskiestIf a part reacts twice to the same message and is not built to ignore the repeat, it can launch a worker twice or open 2 features for 1 idea.

In-memory domain events consumed in the level-triggered reconcile pass; the pass re-derives work from ledger rows.

pros

chosen
A
confidence
high
made_by
step
rationale
The design settles it: fleetd runs 1 level-triggered reconcile pass every 5 s so a missed event is caught on the next pass (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation). The strongest argument against A: 5 s per hop makes a 4-hop chain such as F2 take up to 20 s.
would_flip_if
Latency of a pass hop becomes visible to the operator The ledger becomes event-sourced (strategize Q2) A consumer side effect cannot be made idempotent

kind
ownership
options

pros

cons
task-execution gains process code
risks

B worker-profiles: the wrapper builds the config home and maps CLI events per adapter.
pros
Adapter knowledge is in 1 place
cons
Attempt facts then cross R10 back to task-execution
risks
worker-profiles grows a runtime role

referenced by connect › decisions D2

C fleet-runtime: the wrapper is process supervision through the platform layer.
pros
Platform code stays in 1 context
cons
fleet-runtime must know CLI event formats
risks
fleet-runtime stops being a thin generic layer (strategize N1)

Referenced nowhere else.

rationale
Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. The design names the wrapper as a component but not a context. Recommendation: B, because the wrapper's variable part is per CLI adapter; the strongest argument against it is that heartbeat facts feed the task-execution lease every 10 s. The orchestrator chose B, the recommendation of this step. Reason of the orchestrator: the wrapper is the profile made real (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping), and the scrub needs 1 owner. Process group and kill go through the platform interface, which each context calls. This differs from the recommendation of the code step (fleet-runtime).
would_flip_if
The wrapper holds lease logic The adapters move into fleet-runtime

whatWe decided who owns each part of fleetd and how many separate programs ship.
decided1 team (the operator and the AI agents) owns all 6 parts. All 6 parts ship in 1 program, the horch binary, as separate modules. The OS code sits in 1 library inside it (crates/horch-platform), and docs sync is a horch command inside it too.
assumedEach part keeps its own database tables and folders inside that 1 program, and no part edits another part's tables.
riskiest1 team owns 6 parts, 2 of them core. An arch_scan rule checks the module walls; if the rule is weak, the parts tangle and a later split costs much more.

1 stream-aligned team, core-team, owns all 6 contexts: the operator and the fleet of AI agents (manifest scale_target notes; understand N6; strategize N3). The size is not recorded because the number of agents changes from run to run and has no cap (understand C13).

high

Decision D1 records the options.

notes
1 human operator plus a changing number of AI agents (no cap, understand C13). Runs the horch binary on the operator's machine; reached through the horch CLI, herdr panes and the needs-you list. Load is high because the team owns 6 contexts and 2 core contexts. Mitigation: no second team exists, so keep each context a module with its own tables and folders, enforce the boundaries with an arch_scan rule (A11), give an agent 1 context per task where possible, and add the contexts in the 9 migration phases.

rationale
fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI, the daemon and the wrapper always have the same version and horch self-update restarts the daemon on the new binary (design: Amendments D9, FM-34; understand C1). All 13 relationships are in-process calls and events (connect N1), task-execution reaches worker-profiles and fleet-runtime with synchronous calls (connect F2, F4), and 1 team owns every context. No split reason is in the inputs. Released through horch self-update and the GitHub release assets (understand C7). The platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform, linked into this binary (A9). Docs sync is a horch subcommand of this binary (D2, A10). worker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper role (A3).

ideas Ideas
purpose
Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (worker-profiles). It owns the 1 needs-you list, where everything that waits for the operator is shown.

evolution
custom
domain_roles
specification-model approver
domain_roles_rationale
It builds a document, the plan, that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3) and then executed by task-execution: a specification model. It holds the operator approval gate, where an idea goes on only with the operator's approved hash (FR-10, I7): an approver. Decision D2 took option A (orchestrator, D15; [define A18]).

ubiquitous_language
Idea
definition
A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it
avoid
ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea) request
Sub-Orchestrator
definition
The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase
avoid
orchestrator lead
Assumption
definition
1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11)
avoid
requirement
Plan
definition
The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan
avoid
ticket list
Spec
definition
spec.md and requirements.yaml of 1 idea. Every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. It is written only after approval, in the phase specifying (FR-10).
Question
definition
A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator
Orchestrator
definition
Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3)
Needs-you list
definition
The 1 place for everything that waits for the operator (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/): approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15)
business_decisions
Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12). An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5). The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification. While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/. When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator). A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12). Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3). A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded. After 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, the question escalates to the needs-you list, and the wait for the operator has no limit (RR-12, [define A29]). The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, so fleetd stays the only ledger writer. When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned. When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4). Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles start-agent-process (connect N3, [define A30]). There is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. Approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks (task-escalated from task-execution) wait there for the operator; no other context shows the operator an item to decide (design OR-3, [define A25]).
assumptions
[understand A3] horch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage. (confidence medium) [understand A7] The alternatives are inferred from the design and the research files: today's horch with 1 orchestrator conversation, agents run by hand, and hosted merge queues (GitHub merge queue, bors, Mergify). (confidence medium) [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high) [discover A2] The idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1, option A, decided by the orchestrator, D15). (confidence high) [discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow (decision D2, option B, decided by the orchestrator, D15). The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline. (confidence high) [discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high) [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high) [discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low) [discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high) [decompose A2] The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A3] The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Decision D2, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A4] Worker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 3 of their events (discover H14, N10). Decision D3, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15): approvals, interview questions, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts it on the list. (confidence high) [decompose A11] worker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started: it starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment of the profile (discover N10). This keeps the environment scrub with 1 owner (decision D3). verification_metrics
Business (G3): count of tasks that exist outside a committed, validated plan, plus count of processes that planned 2 ideas at once. Target 0. Business (G3): count of ideas past awaiting_approval whose approved_sha256 does not match the current assumptions.md (I7). Target 0. Structural: count of ledger writes to ideas, plans or questions tables that come from code outside the ideas module (organise N2). Target 0. Structural: count of items shown to the operator for a decision from outside the needs-you list of ideas ([define A25]). Target 0.
open_questions
[understand Q8] This repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10), and plan validation refuses a project with no declared fast gate. Which command is the fast gate of this repository? Proposed answer (orchestrator, D15): the workspace tests without the crate horch-e2e. A run must confirm it. [discover Q3] Does an operator requeue also restore the single replan (H12)? Answered part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0, and a requeue by a review keeps its own counter. [discover H2 near feature-opened - conflict] 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)? [discover H3 near sub-orchestrator-started - conflict] 'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3). [discover H7 near idea-captured - unclear] The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it? Answered (orchestrator, D15): the idea gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. [discover H10 near question-escalated - unclear] A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours. Answered (orchestrator, D15): 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, as a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit. [connect CC2 - coupling, medium] ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas. [connect CC3 - coupling, medium] ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back. [connect CC8 - coupling, medium] plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons. [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.

task-execution Task execution
purpose
Task execution decides which worker runs each ready task, holds every attempt to an earned lease, and decides from facts on disk when a task is done, so that no task stalls silently (G1) and the subscription usage is used fully (G4). It serves the sub-orchestrator and the operator: they see each task verified done or escalated with a reason. It does not plan tasks (ideas), keep worktrees (worktree-custody), land branches (integration), or build launch environments and start processes (worker-profiles).

domain_roles_rationale
It owns the task, attempt and verification aggregates and moves them through state machines with real invariants (I1, I2, I4, I5, RR-2, RR-3). Policies and the clock drive almost all of its 17 commands; the worker, agent CLI and provider pool inputs pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]), not a gateway role.

ubiquitous_language
Task
definition
A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1)
avoid
job claim
Attempt
definition
1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd
avoid
run session
Lease
definition
The time-limited hold of 1 attempt on its task. It renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota (discover N1)
avoid
claim lock
Fallback
definition
The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage
avoid
backup model
Judge Task
definition
A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5)
avoid
review task judgment task
Resolver Task
definition
A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files
avoid
merge task
Check
definition
The acceptance command of a task. The verifier runs it in the worktree, in the sandbox profile of the worker
Done
definition
A task state that only the verifier sets, from facts on disk. It does not mean landed or merged (understand N4)
Ready
definition
A task state: every dependency is done and the task waits for dispatch (discover N6)
Feature
definition
A code kind of a task (with quality, refactor and security). It is not the feature of the integration context (discover N2)
Verification
definition
The check of 1 attempt's result that decides done: result.json validates, the task check passes in the worker's sandbox, and the review (code kinds) or the paired judge (judgment kinds) passes. It is the only writer of done.
business_decisions
Only the verifier moves a task to done. A task is done only when result.json exists and validates, and its check passes when fleetd runs it in the worker's sandbox; a code kind also needs today's review scripts to pass, and a judgment kind needs its judge task to report no open CRITICAL item (RR-3, SR-4, understand N4, discover N4). When a plan is committed, every task whose dependencies are all done becomes ready; no task is ready while a dependency is not done (I2). A refused plan escalates its tasks. fleetd pushes each ready task to a worker: it leases the task, asks worktree-custody for the worktree, writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md, then launches the attempt. A worker never searches for work (FR-5). A lease renews only when the process is alive, the wrapper heartbeat is under 30 s old, and activity happened within stall_after (default 300 s). An expired lease ends the attempt; a task never stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1). The herdr agent status (agent-status-changed) is 1 liveness signal; it never sets a state by itself ([define A23]). Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. A sleep never expires a lease (PL-4). Stall ladder: idle_no_result gets the constant doorbell once, again 2 min later; still idle or hung ends the attempt with outcome stalled; waiting_approval ends the attempt and marks the profile unhealthy; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result. A reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 ledger transaction before any signal is sent (04 S7). The stop signals only the recorded PID with its start time, and refuses a worker of another host (04 S8). A usage limit or a provider outage is not a stall and burns no attempt. If the persona's fallback is on another provider, the task restarts at once on the fallback persona in the same worktree; else it waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused until the pool resets (RR-11). fleetd paces dispatch to each pool's usage window so that the usage is consumed by the reset (OR-4, 06 S13). The target of full use is open (understand Q1). Any non-verified outcome retries after a backoff of 30 s, 2 min, then 8 min in the same worktree, with a handoff file, while attempts remain under the profile's max_attempts. Then the task goes to its sub-orchestrator for 1 replan, then task-escalated puts it on the needs-you list of ideas (RR-6, [define A25]). An operator requeue of a held task sets its attempt count to 0 (attempt_floor, 04 L8); a requeue by a review keeps its own counter ([define A28]). A task parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree and its dependents stay blocked (04 L5 with integration). No 2 running tasks of 1 feature own overlapping paths, and an exclusive task runs alone (04 L6). A judge verdict with an open CRITICAL item opens a fix in a fresh session; after 2 fix rounds with a CRITICAL item left, the task escalates to the operator. A HIGH finding goes to the sub-orchestrator to fix or dismiss. A second judge raises no new MEDIUM or LOW item (FR-4, FM-33, discover N5). A worker that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write the result; the wrapper does this, not the model. When a question is answered, or the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, the parked task resumes its worker session with the answer; if the resume fails, a fresh worker starts from the question, the answer and the committed work (RR-12). A failed rescue of the task's worktree escalates the task; nothing is removed (RR-9). A task branch that conflicts on landing goes back to the same worker. Task branches rebase at landing: a rebase of the feature branch does not wait for running attempts, and an attempt on an old base meets its conflict at landing ([define A27]). No worker runs more than 1 attempt at a time (I4). Every live pane and process under the fleet belongs to a live attempt; anything else is stopped (I5). Every launch calls worker-profiles start-agent-process, which resolves the launch environment and starts the process; this context never builds an environment or starts a process itself (connect N3, decompose N8, [define A30]). No process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). task-execution and integration are a partnership: task-done, task-escalated, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened change together as versioned in-memory events, and a change of 1 state machine is planned with the other (connect N6, [define A24]).
assumptions
[understand A4] The design gives no number for full use of the subscription usage. G4 uses a proxy: no pool ends its window with usage left while a task is ready, and a usage limit burns 0 attempts. (confidence low) [understand A5] A judge, a resolver and a triage agent are workers that run a task of a given kind. They are not separate actors. (confidence medium) [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high) [discover A5] The judge, resolver and triage workers are the 'worker' actor running a task of a given kind (understand A5). (confidence medium) [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high) [discover A7] 'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event. (confidence medium) [discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low) [discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high) [discover A11] A state name is never written without the kind of its entity (design A20). The shared names stay: ready (task, task branch, feature) and landed (task branch, worktree). A task is done; its task branch is landed. (confidence high) [decompose A2] The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium) [decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. verification_metrics
Business (G1): minutes from a worker going idle on a held task until fleetd retries or escalates it. Target under 10 min (about 7 min by design). Business (G1): count of tasks left assigned with an expired lease, from check_invariants I1. Target 0. Business (G4): attempts burned by a usage limit or a provider outage. Target 0. Structural: count of code paths outside the verification module that set a task to done (notes N1). Target 0.
open_questions
[understand Q1] What number counts as full use of the subscription usage for G4: a share of each pool window consumed by its reset, or a count of ready tasks left waiting while a pool has usage? [understand Q7] Is 100 changed lines or 2 files the right size limit for a resolver task, and how accurate is a structural merge tool on the recorded conflicts of this repository? [discover Q3] Does an operator requeue also restore the single replan (H12)? Answered part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0, and a requeue by a review keeps its own counter. [decompose Q2] Docs sync and adapter conformance are stormed as 2 events only (discover H14). Which context turns a drift into a task, and how does a profile become healthy again? [discover H1 near attempt-launched - conflict] Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity). Readers of today's ledger and code will read 'task' where fleetd means 'attempt' (understand N1). [discover H4 near task-done - conflict] 'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4). [discover H5 near judge-verdict-written - conflict] 'Judgment kind' (research, design, docs, report, creative) and the kind 'judge' sound alike. A judgment task needs a paired judge task; a judge task needs no judge. A resolver task has a code kind. Mixing them breaks plan validation (understand N12). [discover H9 near task-leased - unclear] What number counts as 'full use' of the subscription usage that pacing aims for? Pacing holds dispatch per pool window, but the design gives no target (understand Q1). [discover H12 near task-requeued - unclear] A task gets max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then goes to the operator. A requeue resets attempt_floor (04 L8). Does a requeued task also get a new replan, and how does the 2-requeue limit of the review scripts count against attempts? Answered in part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0; a review requeue keeps its own counter. The replan stays open (Q3). [discover H13 near lease-expired - risk] Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake. [connect CC1 - coupling, high] task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other. [connect CC2 - coupling, medium] ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas. [connect CC4 - coupling, medium] task-execution and worktree-custody depend on each other (R4 and R5): the worktree lifecycle follows the task lease and the attempt end, and launch waits for the worktree. [connect CC5 - coupling, medium] task-leased is an event, but task-execution cannot launch until the worktree exists, and a failed git worktree add must come back to task-execution. The event hides a command that needs a result. [connect CC8 - coupling, medium] plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons.

worktree-custody Worktree custody
purpose
Worktree custody owns every worktree from the moment it is reserved to the moment it is removed, so that no work a worker paid for is lost (G2). It decides when a worktree may be created, reused, rescued or removed, and it reconciles the ledger, the work directory and git on every pass. It serves task-execution, which gets a worktree for each leased task. It does not land or delete branches (integration) and does not decide task states (task-execution).

domain
supporting

cost-reducer
evolution
custom

domain_roles_rationale
It owns the worktree aggregate, whose lifecycle (reserved, created, landing, landed, orphaned, removed) protects invariant I6 and rescue rule RR-9. The clock and policies drive its 4 commands; no person commands it.

ubiquitous_language
Worktree
definition
The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued
avoid
checkout workspace
Rescue Ref
definition
A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase
avoid
backup archive ref (a different ref family)
Worktree Lease
definition
Same as Lease in this context: the worktree row that holds 1 worktree for 1 task and 1 owner. It is not the attempt lease of task-execution (decompose N4).
Orphan
definition
A worktree, on disk or in git worktree list, that the ledger does not own or whose owner attempt is dead. It is adopted or rescued, never deleted.
Lease
definition
The worktree lease: the ledger row written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. It holds the worktree for 1 task until its work is landed or rescued
Landed
definition
A worktree state: nothing in the worktree is unique any more, so fleetd may remove it (discover N6)
Orphaned
definition
A worktree on disk with no live owner attempt, or with no ledger row
business_decisions
A worktree row is written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees (FR-11). A row left in reserved by a crash is created or dropped on the next pass. No worktree is removed until its commits, its uncommitted files and its untracked files are saved on a rescue ref under refs/horch/rescue/, and that ref is read back and shown to hold them (RR-9). A rescue that fails verification leaves the tree in place and escalates the task. Every pass compares the ledger with the work directory, and git worktree list every 60 s. A worktree on disk with no row, or with no live owner attempt, is adopted or rescued within 1 pass and never deleted (RR-10, I6). Drop and cleanup refuse a dirty tree, a branch with a git stash entry, unpublished unique commits, and a HEAD that moved during the checks (04 W6). Archive and trash refs only move forward, each ref write is read back before a folder is removed, and trash refs expire after 30 days (04 W8). Triage commits modified and untracked files before ARCHIVE or DELETE (04 W9). A worktree survives attempts: a retry, a fallback restart or a resume reuses the same worktree (understand N1). The worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch landed; only a landed or rescued worktree is removed (decompose N6). An abandoned task branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued is recorded (connect N4). No git call runs inside a ledger transaction. worktree-custody is the only caller of git worktree add, remove and list, and the only writer of rescue refs under refs/horch/rescue/. It runs no rebase, merge or branch delete; integration does ([define A26]).
assumptions

integration Landing and integration
purpose
Integration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for its pull request, so that each idea reaches the primary branch through its own feature (G3) and no landing overwrites other work (G2). It serves the operator, who merges 1 tested pull request per feature, and the sub-orchestrator, which gets conflicts as resolver tasks. It finds conflicts between features early by trial merges and keeps each feature branch rebased. It does not verify tasks (task-execution) and does not remove worktrees or write rescue refs (worktree-custody).

ubiquitous_language
Feature
definition
1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas (understand N2). The feature aggregate owns feature-opened to feature-merged (discover N2)
avoid
project epic
Feature Branch
definition
The branch of 1 feature that collects its landed task branches and reaches the primary branch through 1 pull request
avoid
integration branch
Task Branch
definition
The branch of 1 task that lands on its feature branch through the landing state machine
avoid
worker branch
Primary Branch
definition
The base branch of a project; main in this repository, not in every project
avoid
main master trunk
Bundle
definition
1 candidate made from the feature branch tip plus every ready task branch of that feature, tested once by the fast gate
avoid
batch merge train
Fast Gate
definition
The declared unit-test command of a project that every bundle and every rebased feature branch must pass
avoid
CI check
Full Gate
definition
The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests, run on a feature tip over the current primary branch; a pass goes stale when either tip moves
avoid
CI e2e run
Trial Merge
definition
A merge-tree result between 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, recorded in the ledger with no checkout
avoid
dry run
Resolver Task
definition
A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files
avoid
merge task
Ready
definition
A task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle. A feature is ready when its full gate passed and its pull request can open (discover N6)
Landed
definition
A task branch state: the branch is fast-forwarded onto its feature branch after the fast gate passed (understand N4)
Merged
definition
A feature fact read from git by content: the feature branch is in the primary branch (understand N4)
Trial merge result
definition
The answer of a git merge-tree trial merge between 2 features, or a feature and the primary branch: clean, or the conflicting paths. Coined in connect (assumption A6)
business_decisions
A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2). A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch. On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator. Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9). A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5). Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11). A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]). Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10); worktree-custody writes it ([define Q6]). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12). When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7). When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task. The rebase does not wait for the running attempts of the feature; their task branches rebase at landing ([define A27]). When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature. A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default. A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9). An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4). integration is the only caller of the git branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete. It runs no git worktree command and writes no rescue ref; worktree-custody does ([define A26]). integration and task-execution are a partnership: their 4 messages change together as versioned in-memory events (connect N6, [define A24]).

Business (G2): count of branches deleted while not landed, merged or rescued, or named by a git stash entry (I12). Target 0. Business (G3): count of features marked merged whose changes are not in the primary branch by content (I8). Target 0. Business (G3): share of landed task branches that hit a conflict. open_questions
[understand Q1] What number counts as full use of the subscription usage for G4: a share of each pool window consumed by its reset, or a count of ready tasks left waiting while a pool has usage? [understand Q7] Is 100 changed lines or 2 files the right size limit for a resolver task, and how accurate is a structural merge tool on the recorded conflicts of this repository? [understand Q8] This repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10), and plan validation refuses a project with no declared fast gate. Which command is the fast gate of this repository? Proposed answer (orchestrator, D15): the workspace tests without the crate horch-e2e. A run must confirm it. [discover H2 near feature-opened - conflict] 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)? [discover H6 near task-branch-verified - conflict] 'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed. [discover H8 near task-branch-landed - risk] The Preservation analysis rows (04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10, M5, 05 E-10, 06 S1 to S15) are hard inputs. Each must have exactly 1 owner in the model; a row that falls between 2 owners is a behavior fleetd silently drops (understand N15). [discover H11 near fast-gate-passed - external] Plan validation refuses a project that has not declared a fast gate and a full gate, and this repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10, understand Q8). Until one is declared, no plan of this repository can commit. [discover H15 near pull-request-merged - external] A project setting says who merges a feature; the default is the operator. When the setting lets fleetd merge, which gate and which actor stands for the merge decision? [connect CC1 - coupling, high] task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other. [connect CC3 - coupling, medium] ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back. [connect CC6 - coupling, high] Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer. [connect CC7 - coupling, high] abandon-task-branch drops a task branch in integration, but the rescue ref that keeps the work is made in worktree-custody (04 W6). Both must happen, in order, or work is lost. [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.
