worker-profiles Worker profiles and adapters
purpose
Worker profiles turns 1 named worker profile into the exact CLI, flags, environment, config files and sandbox of each agent launch, so that every agent runs on the operator's subscription logins and never with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (C2). It serves ideas and task-execution, which ask it to start each agent process: it resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper and starts it through the platform layer. It keeps the adapters of every agent CLI correct by docs sync and conformance tests, and marks a profile unhealthy when its adapter fails. It does not choose which task runs (task-execution).

domain_roles_rationale
Every launch of every context passes through start-agent-process and its launch environment, which apply the environment scrub and the login rules (decompose N2, N8, connect N3). It ensures that other contexts carry out the operator's credential rule: an enforcer. It owns 1 aggregate, the worker profile, with few commands, and the fleet-run wrapper ([define A30]).

ubiquitous_language
Worker Profile
definition
The teammate file of 1 persona: agent CLI, model, effort, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, network, liveness, retry and fallback. Profile is its short name.
Adapter
definition
The code for 1 agent CLI that turns a worker profile into the exact flags, environment and files of a launch, and reads its quota and context.
Persona
definition
A named worker profile that a plan task names. Every worker persona names a fallback persona on another provider when the roster has one.
Conformance
definition
The test that launches 1 adapter and reads back its effective settings (sandbox, context limit, hooks, scrubbed environment). A pass makes the profile healthy.
Profile
definition
A named worker profile: the CLI, model, effort, sandbox and permission rules that 1 attempt runs with
Healthy
definition
A profile whose adapter passed its last conformance test. Dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile
Launch environment
definition
The exact CLI, flags, scrubbed environment, config home files and sandbox profile that worker-profiles resolves for 1 process launch. Coined in connect (assumption A6)
Start agent process
definition
The worker-profiles call that starts the fleet-run wrapper of 1 attempt, or 1 sub-orchestrator pane, in its own process group through the platform layer. Coined in connect (assumption A6)
Fleet-run wrapper
definition
The horch process role that runs 1 attempt: it sets the private config home, scrubs the environment, maps adapter events and writes heartbeat.json and exit.json (connect A7)
business_decisions
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is removed from the environment of every launch: attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, detached child, updater and probe. The roster rejects a teammate file that sets it (05 E-10, 06 S1, understand N16, decompose N2). agy children lose GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, and the roster rejects them (06 S3). Secrets reach agents only through env vars that the profile names, never through task files (SR-2). A profile must declare CLI, model, skills, MCP servers, sandbox, writable paths, context budget, timeouts and restart policy, and every worker persona must name a fallback persona; the roster refuses an incomplete profile (FR-6). A sandboxed persona does not start on a host that cannot sandbox it (06 S9). Each worker writes only to its task directory, its worktree and the paths its profile names (SR-1). When an adapter conformance test fails, its profile is marked unhealthy, and dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile until a conformance test passes. A waiting_approval stall also marks the profile unhealthy. The private CODEX_HOME links every entry of the real codex home except rules/, the Prime agent dir links auth.json, and every codex launch gets --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust (06 S4, S5, S6). Trust writes stay narrow (06 S10). A new agent CLI release is used only after the update cooldown of more than 1 week; a CLI with unreadable release dates is held back. Pane auto-update stays off for claude and codex (06 S7, S8, C10). Each agent runs with a context limit of 256k tokens, set through the CLI's own setting where one exists; else the wrapper ends the attempt with a handoff at 256k (FR-9). The OpenCode, pi and Prime adapters carry over (06 S15). Every agent process starts through start-agent-process: worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper (private config home, environment scrub, adapter event mapping) in its own process group or job object through the platform layer, and never inside a ledger transaction (connect N3, N4, [define A30]). The fleet-run wrapper writes heartbeat.json and exit.json of its attempt with atomic writes. fleetd reads heartbeat-written into task-execution as a file, idempotently (connect A7, RR-8).

fleet-runtime Fleet runtime
purpose
Fleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops silently and no work is lost on a restart (G1, G2). It provides every other context with the single ledger writer, the command channel and the herdr adapter. It decides when fleetd is hung or old and restarts it. It does not own the platform layer, which each context calls directly, and it does not start agent processes (worker-profiles). It does not decide the rows of other contexts' tables (organise N2) or any task, idea, worktree or branch state.
strategic_classification
domain
supporting
business_model
cost-reducer
evolution
custom
domain_roles
gateway execution-context
domain_roles_rationale
It wraps the OS service managers and herdr for the daemon, through the platform layer, and translates them for core code: a gateway. It also executes the daemon lifecycle (heartbeat, hang restart, binary restart, schema migration): an execution context with no domain aggregate.

ubiquitous_language
fleetd
definition
The supervised daemon role of the horch binary (horch fleetd): the only ledger writer, which runs the reconcile pass of all 6 contexts every 5 s (organise N1).
Heartbeat
definition
The time of fleetd's last full pass, written after each pass. horch fleetd check reads it. It is not the wrapper heartbeat.json of an attempt.
Platform Layer
definition
The leaf crate crates/horch-platform: 1 interface with 1 module per OS (mac.rs, linux.rs, windows.rs) for process facts, process group stop, service install and restart, hang detection, file watching, sandboxing, sleep and wake, the command channel transport and the machine probe (PL-2, A19). It is not a bounded context; each context calls it (decompose N7).
Command Channel
definition
The local transport on which CLI commands and agents send requests to fleetd. fleetd validates each request and writes the result to the ledger.
Ledger
definition
The SQLite file ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3 in WAL mode: an event log plus derived tables. Only fleetd writes it; each context owns its own tables (understand N17, organise N2).
Check
definition
horch fleetd check: the heartbeat check that restarts fleetd when its last full pass is older than 30 s of awake time. It is not a task check
business_decisions
Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5). fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5, 06 S14, [define A33]). When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7). Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4). Production code of the workspace has no OS cfg outside the leaf crate crates/horch-platform. Every context, fleet-runtime too, calls its 1 interface, and an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value that the caller decides on (PL-2, PL-3, [define A32]). Phase P moves the 178 existing production sites with no change of behavior (D16, PL-6). New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5). Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8). The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2). No git call or process start runs inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). After a herdr restart, fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files (C14). Agent processes start through worker-profiles (connect N3). Worker reports reach fleetd as files, not through the Unix-socket channel relay or report socket, so Windows loses no report (06 S11).

In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline. C4Context
  title System context - fleetd: the horch fleet control plane
  Person(operator, "Operator", "The developer who drops ideas into the queue, answers interviews, approves assumptions, receives escalations and merges each feature's pull request")
  System_Ext(sub_orchestrator, "Sub-orchestrator", "An interactive Claude Code process, 1 per feature, a fresh process per phase, that plans 1 idea at a time and answers its workers' questions")
  System_Ext(worker, "Worker", "Any agent CLI started with a named profile for 1 attempt of 1 task in a worktree that fleetd leased to it; also runs judge, resolver and triage tasks")
  Person(friend, "Friend", "A person who installs horch and gets each release through horch self-update")
  System(fleetd, "fleetd: the horch fleet control plane", "A supervised daemon inside horch that takes rough ideas from the operator, runs AI coding agents on them, and keeps every task, worktree and branch accounted for until the work reaches the primary branch.")
  System_Ext(clock, "Clock", "The fleetd reconcile pass (every 5 s) and the fixed timers it reads. It fires every time-triggered command. Time counts only while the machine is awake.")
  System_Ext(agent_cli, "Agent CLI process", "The Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, pi or Prime process of 1 attempt. Its exit is a process fact that the wrapper and the platform layer report.")
  System_Ext(git, "git", "Worktrees, branches, refs and merge-tree trial merges. The source of truth for 'in the primary branch by content'.")
  System_Ext(github, "GitHub", "Hosts the pull request of a feature (pr setting gh) or the compare URL (pr setting manual).")
  System_Ext(os_service_manager, "OS service manager", "launchd, systemd, or a Windows service and Task Scheduler. Keeps fleetd and herdr running and restarts them.")
  System_Ext(provider_pool, "Provider pool", "A usage pool of 1 provider (understand actor provider-pool). It reports usage limits, outages and window resets.")
  System_Ext(herdr, "herdr", "The pane runtime in session 'fleet'. Shows panes, agent status and notifications. Holds no state that fleetd depends on.")

quality_attributes12
correctness
context

requirement
A task reaches done only from the verifier, from facts on disk (RR-3).
priority
high
scenario
When a worker writes done in its transcript but leaves no valid result.json, then the task stays not-done and the attempt ends as no_result within 1 pass (5 s).
fault-tolerance
context
task-execution
requirement
A stalled worker loses its lease and its task is retried or escalated; no task stays assigned with an expired lease (RR-1, RR-2, I1).
priority
high
scenario
When a worker process is stopped with kill -STOP during an attempt, then the alarm fires within 1 lease (120 s after stall_after) and the task is retried or escalated.
recoverability
context

priority
high

When fleetd is killed in the middle of a reap, then after restart the attempt is ended and the task requeued exactly once, and outcomes equal a clean run.
availability

high

When a worker's pool reports a usage limit, then its attempt count does not change and the task restarts on the fallback persona at once or waits until the pool resets.

whatThis step turns the 6 parts of the fleetd design into a code plan for Rust: which folders, which types, which interfaces, which tests, and in which order to build them. It writes no code.
decidedAll 6 parts live as modules under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/. The OS-specific code lives in its own small crate, crates/horch-platform, that every part calls. 3 parts get aggregates (rich objects that guard their own rules): Task and Verification in task-execution, Feature and TaskBranch in integration, and Plan in ideas. An attempt lives inside its task, so a crash can never end the attempt and forget the task. worker-profiles starts every agent process and owns the per-attempt wrapper. The build order is the 9 phases of the design, with Phase P (moving the OS code) right after Phase 0.
assumedWe assumed the existing modules stay where they are and get wrapped, not moved. We also assumed nothing else may mark a task done: only the verifier can create the value that does it. Integration asks worktree-custody for each rescue ref instead of writing it itself.
riskiestWrapping old modules means 2 code paths live side by side until each phase removes the old one. If a phase forgets to remove its old path, the old watchdog and the new fleetd can both act on 1 task. Phase P moves 178 OS-specific sites at once; its only safety net is that every test gives the same result before and after the move.

Path Claim

state_transitions
pending -> ready (promote-task, every dependency done) ready -> leased (dispatch-task, lease and worktree row in 1 transaction) leased -> running (launch-attempt, after worktree-created) running -> running (renew-lease, earned activity only) running -> stalled (renew-lease lease-expired, or apply-stall-ladder) running -> verifying (attempt exit with a result file; write-result alone never leaves verifying) running -> waiting_quota (move-to-fallback with no fallback on another provider) running -> leased (move-to-fallback onto a fallback persona; attempt count unchanged) running -> blocked_on_user (worker question; exec worker exits and the task parks) waiting_quota -> ready (promote-task on quota-window-reset) blocked_on_user -> leased (question-answered or own-assumption-recorded) stalled|verifying -> failed (end-attempt with a non-verified outcome) failed -> ready (schedule-retry while attempts remain) failed -> escalated (escalate-task after the replan, or rescue-failed) verifying -> done (mark-task-done with a VerifiedVerdict only) escalated -> ready (requeue-task by the operator, attempt_floor reset) any non-terminal -> cancelled (plan change) rejected: done from any state without a VerifiedVerdict rejected: ready while a dependency is not done rejected: leased for a worker that already runs an attempt (I4)

domain_services
DispatchPlanner
description
Picks ready tasks for workers across Task instances: I4, path overlap (04 L6), exclusive tasks, health guards and pool pacing. Pure: takes snapshots and a Clock reading.
StallLadder
description
Maps a liveness snapshot (process alive, heartbeat age, activity age, agent state) and an awake-time reading to the next rung: doorbell, doorbell, end.
application_services
PromoteTask
command
promote-task
description
pending to ready when every dependency is done, or waiting_quota to ready when the pool resets.
DispatchTask
command
dispatch-task
description
No cap. Only the health guards (free disk, load) and the pacing of the pool hold dispatch.
LaunchAttempt
command
launch-attempt
description
Starts the wrapper and the CLI in its own process group. A resume after an answer also launches. Asks LaunchEnvironmentGateway, then AgentProcessGateway, after the ledger transaction commits (connect N3, N4).
RenewLease
command
renew-lease
description
Every reconcile pass (5 s). Lease time counts only while the machine is awake.
ApplyStallLadder
command
apply-stall-ladder
description
Every pass: doorbell, doorbell after 2 min, then end. stall_after default 5 min; start timeout 90 s.
MoveToFallback
command
move-to-fallback
description
Fallback persona on another provider, else waiting_quota with the lease paused.
WriteResult
command
write-result
description
horch result writes outbox/result.json. Records the result on the Attempt. It never moves the task to done (define N1).
RunCheck
command
run-check
description
The verifier, with today's check timeout (20 min, max 24 h).
RunReview
command
run-review
description
Today's review scripts, unchanged. Rounds: light 1, full 3.
WriteJudgeVerdict
command
write-judge-verdict
description
The worker of a judge task writes its verdict file.
OpenCriticalFix
command
open-critical-fix
description
At most 2 fix rounds.
SettleHighFinding
command
settle-high-finding
description
Fix or dismiss with a written reason.
EndAttempt
command
end-attempt
description
Stops the process group through the platform layer (Linux: SIGINT, 20 s, SIGKILL).
ScheduleRetry
command
schedule-retry
description
Reads max_attempts and backoff from the profile.
EscalateTask
command
escalate-task
description
Publishes task-escalated with its reason. ideas puts the task on the 1 needs-you list (A14).
RequeueTask
command
requeue-task
description
Resets attempt_floor.
MarkTaskDone

mark-task-done
description
The verifier writes verdict.json. Takes a VerifiedVerdict; only the verification module can construct one (D4).

building -> verifying (task enters verifying) verifying -> ready (mark-branch-ready on task-done) ready -> in_bundle (build-bundle, queue order) in_bundle -> conflicted (build-bundle, rebase conflict; the task goes back to its worker) in_bundle -> landed (fast-forward-feature-branch after fast-gate-passed, under the land lock) in_bundle -> gate_failed (bisect-bundle finds it; open-triage-task) conflicted -> verifying (a new attempt of the same worker) gate_failed -> verifying (triage task fixed) any -> abandoned (abandon-task-branch by the operator, after worktree-rescued) rejected: ready while the task is not done rejected: landed for a cancelled task (04 F9) rejected: deletion without landed, merged or rescued

decisions4
D1 Where do the 6 context modules live in the existing crates?mediumfoundation
kind
foundation
options
A New modules crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain, application and adapters; existing modules b…

New modules crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain, application and adapters; existing modules become adapters behind the new ports.

pros
Matches understand N6: contexts are modules inside horch-core Clear seam for the fitness tests Existing tests of taskledger and vcs keep running while phases land
cons
2 code paths exist until each phase retires the old one Adapters wrap code that is not hexagonal
risks
Old and new paths drift if a phase leaves the old one in place

referenced by code › decisions D1

B Evolve existing modules in place: taskledger becomes task-execution, vcs becomes integration, and so on.
pros
No wrapper code 1 code path at all times
cons
Existing modules mix concerns of several contexts (taskledger holds worktrees, landing and tasks) No place for the dependency rule
risks
A large refactor before Phase 1 can start

Referenced nowhere else.

C A new crate horch-fleetd that horch depends on.
pros
Compiler-enforced boundary to horch-core
cons
Contradicts understand N6 (modules inside horch-core) Cyclic needs: fleetd adapters wrap horch-core modules and horch-core tests need fleetd
risks
Build time and a crate split nobody asked for

Referenced nowhere else.

chosen
A
confidence
medium
rationale
understand N6 puts the contexts inside horch-core, and the migration plan replaces old behaviour phase by phase, so the old modules must keep working behind adapters until their phase retires them.
would_flip_if
The operator wants a crate boundary enforced by the compiler A phase retires a whole existing module at once, so wrapping it costs more than moving it
made_by
step
records

whatThis step wrote 30 contracts: the exact shape of each file or request that crosses a process line in fleetd. These are operator commands, files the sub-orchestrators, workers and the wrapper write, files fleetd writes for them, and facts from git, GitHub, herdr, the agent CLI, the provider and the clock. Each contract has a schema, a good example and bad examples it must reject.
decidedEvery field name is snake_case, as in the design (D1, option B). Each operator command carries an idempotency_key and gets back accepted, or refused with a reason. result.json status is completed, blocked or failed. reset_at is optional.
assumedThe idempotency_key is an opaque string of 1 to 128 characters, because no source gives its format. verdict.json decision is done or ready, from the Verifier row of the design.
riskiestheartbeat-written and task-escalated sit inside 1 deployable, so the checker warns about them. If the wrapper later runs in fleetd itself, heartbeat-written stops being a wire contract.

semantics
1 result per attempt: result.json is written atomically and never rewritten; fleetd ingests it once per (task, attempt). The result is a claim, not a fact: a task is done only when result.json validates and the verifier's check passes in the worker sandbox (RR-3, SR-4). acceptance_self_check is advisory; the verifier never trusts it. A process that exits with commits and no result gets 1 short resume of the same session to write it; an exit without a valid result is outcome no_result. status is 1 of the closed list completed, blocked, failed (orchestrator, D15). The worker's status is a claim; only the verifier moves a task to done.

rationale
Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. The field names are the snake_case names of the design, in each file. Recommendation of this step: B. Strongest argument against: connect and code.json then need a re-run to match. The orchestrator chose B, the recommendation of this step; connect and code adopted the snake_case names in this round, so the risk of 2 vocabularies is gone.

understandA1highLifecycle is brownfield: horch runs in production today, and the design is a set of changes to horch, not a rewrite (design.md, Where multi-herdr stands today, Keep, change, add).
understandA2mediumThe operator is the single primary actor. Friends who install horch through horch self-update are a secondary segment with the same needs and no approval role.
understandA3mediumhorch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage.
understandA4lowThe design gives no number for full use of the subscription usage. G4 uses a proxy: no pool ends its window with usage left while a task is ready, and a usage limit burns 0 attempts.
understandA5mediumA judge, a resolver and a triage agent are workers that run a task of a given kind. They are not separate actors.
understandA6mediumEvolution stages: the control-plane capabilities are custom because no product does them for local agent CLIs; pane hosting is a product (herdr); host platform services are a commodity (each OS provides them).
understandA7mediumThe alternatives are inferred from the design and the research files: today's horch with 1 orchestrator conversation, agents run by hand, and hosted merge queues (GitHub merge queue, bors, Mergify).
understandA8highThe /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3.
understandA9highWhen the design and another source disagree, the design wins. The other sources describe the system of today.
understandA10highMode auto, depth standard, 1 deployable unit and 1 team are fixed by the run. The operator and the AI agents of the fleet count as 1 team.
understandA11highAll 178 existing OS-specific production sites move behind the platform layer in 1 dedicated phase, Phase P, between Phase 0 and Phase 1, with no change of behavior. The cfg sites in test code stay (operator decision D16; design amendment A19).
discoverA1highThe board is to-be: it models fleetd as design.md describes it, not today's horch. Today's differences appear as conflict hotspots H1 to H4 (design.md wins over the other sources, per the run context).
discoverA2highThe idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1, option A, decided by the orchestrator, D15).
discoverA3highDaemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow (decision D2, option B, decided by the orchestrator, D15). The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline.
discoverA4highfleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3).
discoverA5mediumThe judge, resolver and triage workers are the 'worker' actor running a task of a given kind (understand A5).
discoverA6highThe event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned, and bundle states) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, removed, orphaned, rescued), and understand N23 and N24 (the task and feature state machines).
discoverA7medium'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event.
discoverA8lowAn idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7).
discoverA9mediumThe fleetd command channel, request files while fleetd is down, and the herdr pane mapping are design-level transport; they are not on the board. Request classes, the operator token and the requests table are also transport (understand N25).
discoverA10highEvent count 102 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 6 state machines (idea, task, task branch, bundle, feature, worktree) plus jobs; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6.
discoverA11highA state name is never written without the kind of its entity (design A20). The shared names stay: ready (task, task branch, feature) and landed (task branch, worktree). A task is done; its task branch is landed.
decomposeA1highThe 6 contexts are modules inside horch-core in 1 deployable unit and 1 team (understand N6). The boundaries are model boundaries, not process boundaries.
decomposeA2mediumThe verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15).
decomposeA3mediumThe question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Decision D2, option A (orchestrator, D15).
decomposeA4mediumWorker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 3 of their events (discover H14, N10). Decision D3, option A (orchestrator, D15).
decomposeA5mediumWorktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15).
decomposeA6mediumThe ledger is infrastructure that fleet-runtime owns as the single writer. Each context owns the state transitions of its own aggregates; it is not a shared kernel.
decomposeA7highOperator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15): approvals, interview questions, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts it on the list.
decomposeA8highTriage and resolver tasks are opened by integration but run as normal tasks in task-execution; integration asks task-execution for them.
decomposeA9mediumEach preservation row has 1 owning context, as listed in N3. The row texts come from the Preservation analysis of design.md.
decomposeA10highThe platform layer is not a bounded context and has no subdomain. It is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform (design A19, understand N13), and each context calls it directly. fleet-runtime uses it like every other context.
decomposeA11mediumworker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started: it starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment of the profile (discover N10). This keeps the environment scrub with 1 owner (decision D3).
strategizeA1highIdeas stays supporting, not core. Decision D1 took option C (orchestrator, D15): the subdomain is split by module. Plan validation is a domain-model module: it holds the rules of coverage, the DAG, judge pairing, the model guide and the declared gates. Idea intake and worker questions stay active-record. The judgment work (research, interview, assumptions, spec, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model, not by fleetd code. Scored diff 6, cplx 5.
strategizeA2mediumCore stays the minority: 2 of 6 subdomains (task-execution, integration). Ideas would make 3 of 6, which is half, not a minority (ticket rule for this run).
strategizeA3highThe 2 cores use domain-model: state rows are the truth, and the events table is the audit trail that the one door writes beside each row in the same transaction (design, Ledger, rule 1 One door). Decision D2 took option A (orchestrator, D15): a domain model with an events table, not event-sourced.
strategizeA4highFleet runtime is supporting, not generic. Its pane hosting (herdr) and host services (launchd, systemd, Windows service) are adopted and only wrapped, as understand N14 says. The single ledger writer and the command channel have no product to buy, so the subdomain as a whole is built. The platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform (design A19). It is not part of fleet-runtime and has no subdomain (decompose N7).
strategizeA5mediumWorktree custody is supporting with medium investment. Its no-loss rule (rescue ref written and read back before any removal) is 1 invariant over a 8-state lifecycle, not an algorithm; a failure breaks G2, so it gets invariant tests and fault-injection tests. Round 3: the rescue ref has 2 classes (unique, superseded), and each git step is a job (A27, A32); the score stays.
strategizeA6highWorker profiles is supporting with medium investment because it owns the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub (C2, an absolute operator rule). Its complexity is the rate of change of the agent CLIs, not domain rules.
strategizeA7highEvery subdomain has evolution custom: each has at least 1 custom capability. The commodity and product capabilities of fleet-runtime (host services, pane hosting) are adopted systems, not built parts.
connectA1highAll 6 contexts run in the 1 fleetd process, so every context-to-context message is in-process. Only the command channel, the file protocol, the herdr adapter, the platform layer, git and GitHub cross a process boundary (design: Architecture and roles).
connectA2highCross-context events are in-memory events consumed in the level-triggered 5 s reconcile pass, which re-derives work from ledger rows, so a lost event is caught on the next pass. Delivery is at-least-once and every consumer is idempotent on a natural key (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation; decision D1).
connectA3highEvery state change in every flow commits through the single ledger writer in fleet-runtime (decompose N5). The flows do not draw that call on each step.
connectA4highOperator commands travel as horch CLI requests over the fleetd command channel (Unix socket or named pipe, through the platform layer), drawn as via other. When fleetd is down the request goes to a request file that fleetd reads at start (design: The command channel). Each request carries an idempotency_key, and a refusal carries its reason (orchestrator, D15).
connectA5highAgent hand-offs (assumptions.md, plan.yaml, result.json, questions, exit.json) are files: atomic, immutable and read in the pass, so they are at-least-once and idempotent on path and content hash (design: Workspace layout and file protocol).
connectA6high3 message ids were minted here: launch-environment (query), start-agent-process (command) and trial-merge-result (query). Discover adopted all 3 (discover N10): start-agent-process is a discover command, and the 2 queries reuse discover read-model ids.
connectA7highThe fleet-run wrapper belongs to worker-profiles (D2 option B, orchestrator D15). It writes heartbeat.json and exit.json. attempt-exited (exit.json) comes from worker-profiles, the writer of the file; the file records the exit fact of the CLI process.
connectA8highgit is called by 2 contexts, split by concern: worktree-custody for worktrees and rescue refs, integration for branches, merges, bundles and trial merges (orchestrator, D15).
connectA9mediumworker-profiles owns start-agent-process (decompose N8). task-execution and ideas send it; worker-profiles resolves the launch environment, runs the fleet-run wrapper and starts it in its own process group through the platform layer. When the profile needs a pane, the caller gets the pane from the herdr adapter of fleet-runtime (R12, R13) and passes it in the request.
connectA10highEach file of the design workspace layout that crosses the process boundary is 1 message: task.yaml (assign-task), inbox/START.md (start-work), heartbeat.json (heartbeat-written), verdict.json (task-verdict-written), plan.verdict.json (plan-verdict-written) and approval.json (assumptions-approved). The path names its 1 writer (design: Workspace layout and file protocol, rule 3). 6 of these ids are minted here, because discover has no id for them: assign-task, start-work, heartbeat-written, task-verdict-written, plan-verdict-written and agent-status-changed (Q6).
connectA11highPayload field names are the snake_case names of the design (orchestrator, D15). A file message uses the field names of the design example of that file; an in-memory event uses <entity>_id.
connectA12highThe model has 9 flows, 2 more than the 4 to 7 of depth standard. F2 and F3 were split at a hand-off (F8, F9) to keep each flow at 9 messages or fewer after the new file and pull request messages.
organiseA1high1 stream-aligned team, core-team, owns all 6 contexts: the operator and the fleet of AI agents (manifest scale_target notes; understand N6; strategize N3). The size is not recorded because the number of agents changes from run to run and has no cap (understand C13).
organiseA2high1 deployable unit, the horch binary, holds all 6 contexts as modules inside horch-core. The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34; understand C1, N6; decompose N1). Decision D1 records the options.
organiseA3highThe fleet-run wrapper and horch fleetd check are process roles of the same horch binary, not deployables. The design maps the wrapper to today's horch worker subcommand (design: Where multi-herdr stands today) and names horch fleetd check as a horch command (design: Architecture and roles). worker-profiles owns the wrapper (orchestrator, D15; connect D2, connect N3): the wrapper is the profile made real, and the environment scrub has 1 owner. The deployable is the same.
organiseA4mediumThe data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose.
organiseA5highThe questions table belongs to ideas. decompose D2 option A (orchestrator, D15): worker questions belong to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator of the feature answers them. ideas also owns the 1 needs-you list (design OR-3; decompose N9). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, and fleetd stays the only ledger writer.
organiseA6highherdr, the agent CLIs, git, GitHub and the OS service managers are external systems behind adapters in fleet-runtime and the other owning contexts. None is a deployable of this design (strategize N1; design: Architecture and roles).
organiseA7mediumThe cognitive load of core-team is high: 6 contexts and 2 core contexts (task-execution, integration). No second team exists to take a context, so the mitigation is module boundaries that an arch_scan rule enforces (orchestrator, D15), 1 context per task where possible, and the 9 migration phases (Phase 0, Phase P, Phases 1 to 7) that add the contexts one at a time (understand C9, N19).
organiseA8mediumEach context owns its workspace folders inside the 1 deployable: ideas owns the idea folders (ai_docs/plans/<run>/, design /fleet/ideas/), task-execution owns the task and attempt folders under the state root, worker-profiles owns the teammate profile files (understand N17; design: Workspace layout and file protocol).
organiseA9highThe platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform inside the 1 deployable (design A19, D16; understand N13; decompose N7). It is a library crate of the horch workspace, not a bounded context and not a deployable of its own: the horch binary links it, and each context calls it directly. Phase P creates it between Phase 0 and Phase 1 and moves the 178 production OS-specific sites behind it.
organiseA10mediumDocs sync and adapter conformance run as a horch subcommand inside the 1 deployable, and fleetd schedules it daily and on a CLI version change (decision D2 option A, orchestrator, D15). Phase 7 widens crates/herdr-docs-sync into this subcommand. The subcommand reports a drift to ideas as a --direct idea, so ideas creates the task (decompose Q2, answered).
organiseA11highAn arch_scan rule enforces the context boundaries (orchestrator, D15): no context writes or reads the ledger tables or the workspace folders of another context. It sits beside the arch_scan rules of PL-2 (no OS cfg outside crates/horch-platform) and of Phase 5 (every process other than fleetd opens the ledger read-only).

defineA15mediumWorker, wrapper and sub-orchestrator input reaches fleetd only as files of the fleetd file protocol, which ingestion validates and reads idempotently (FR-7, RR-8). So the core contexts guard these inputs with an anticorruption layer, and the pre-fill guesses A4, A5, A7, A8, A10 and A11 hold.
defineA16highfleetd earns no revenue. It saves operator time and paid usage (G1, G2, G4). So the business model of ideas, task-execution, worktree-custody, integration and fleet-runtime is cost-reducer. Decision D1 took option A (orchestrator, D15).
defineA17mediumworker-profiles is a compliance-enforcer: its main value is that every launch obeys the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rule and the login rules (C2, 05 E-10, 06 S1, S3).
defineA18highideas plays the specification-model role (it produces the validated plan that task-execution executes) and the approver role (the operator approval gate, FR-10). Decision D2 took option A (orchestrator, D15).
defineA19mediumintegration receives pull-request-merged from GitHub only as a hint to check sooner. The fact merged is read from git by content (I8, design Between features). connect carries the message since revision round 2 (connect N7).
defineA20mediumintegration sends open-pull-request to GitHub when the project setting pr is gh. With pr manual it pushes the feature branch and shows the compare URL; no GitHub call is made.
defineA21mediumMetric thresholds use the fixed values of the design (pass 5 s, start timeout 90 s, lease 120 s, stall_after 300 s, heartbeat check 30 s). An invariant metric has the target 0 violations.
defineA22highThe define step changes no upstream relationship. Every message id on a canvas comes from connect or discover. The GitHub, herdr and file protocol rows use the connect messages of revision round 2 (connect N7).
defineA23mediumherdr agent status (agent-status-changed) is a liveness hint, never a state. ideas conforms to it for sub-orchestrator panes; task-execution reads it through its anticorruption layer as 1 of its liveness signals (connect N7).
defineA24hightask-execution and integration are a partnership (orchestrator, D15; connect N6). The canvas rows between them carry the pattern partnership, and their 2 state machines change together. decompose R6 and R7 keep their patterns; this step does not edit decompose.
defineA25highThere is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15; design OR-3; decompose N9). task-execution sends task-escalated to ideas, and ideas puts the task on the list beside approvals and escalated questions. No context other than ideas shows an item to the operator for a decision.
defineA26highgit has 2 callers, split by concern (orchestrator, D15). worktree-custody calls git worktree add, remove and list and writes the rescue refs under refs/horch/rescue/. integration calls the branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete.
defineA27highTask branches rebase at landing (orchestrator, D15). A rebase of a feature branch does not wait for the running attempts of the feature. An attempt on an old base meets a conflict at landing, and the task branch goes to conflicted.
defineA28highAn operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0. A requeue by a review keeps its own counter (orchestrator, D15; discover N12).
defineA29mediumA worker question escalates to the operator after 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator. This is a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit (orchestrator, D15; discover N12).
defineA30highworker-profiles owns start-agent-process and the fleet-run wrapper (orchestrator, D15; decompose N8; connect N3). The wrapper is the profile made real: private config home, environment scrub and adapter event mapping. fleet-runtime starts no agent process.
defineA31highideas is split by module (strategize D1 option C, orchestrator, D15). Plan validation is a domain model: coverage, the DAG, judge pairing, the model guide and the declared gates. Intake, the dispatcher and questions stay active-record with invariant tests (strategize N2).
defineA32highThe platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform (design A19). It is not a bounded context, and fleet-runtime does not own it; each context calls it directly (decompose N7). Phase P moves the 178 existing production sites with no change of behavior (D16, PL-6).
defineA33mediumPreservation row 06 S14 (design A21: hang detection and restart on all 3 OSes, not only systemd or launchd) has no owner upstream. fleet-runtime owns it, because it owns the heartbeat check and the restart of fleetd.
codeA1highThe language is Rust. The ticket of this step states it, README.md names it, and every existing crate is Rust. The framework is none: plain Rust with rusqlite for the ledger, as horch-core uses today.
codeA2mediumEach context is 1 module under crates/horch-core/src/fleetd/<context>/ with domain/, application/ and adapters/ submodules (decision D1, understand N6). Existing modules (taskledger, vcs, runtime, roster, harness, routing, workspace) are wrapped by adapters and are not moved in this plan.
codeA3mediumAttempt and its Lease are entities and value objects inside the Task aggregate, not their own aggregate (decision D2), because 04 S7 needs the end of the attempt and the requeue of the task in 1 ledger transaction.
codeA4highOnly the verification module can construct a VerifiedVerdict value, and Task::mark_done takes one; the one-door transition table also refuses verifying -> done with any cause other than verifier (decision D4, define N1).
codeA5highConcurrency inside the ledger needs no optimistic retry: fleetd is the single writer and runs its pass serially (connect D1, design Ledger). Each aggregate still carries a version, and the one-door transition checks from_state, so a stale write fails loudly.
codeA6mediumThe attempts table holds task attempts (written by task-execution) and sub-orchestrator attempts with task_id null (written by ideas). Each context writes only its own row kind (organise N2).
codeA7highThe platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform with its root at crates/horch-platform/src/: lib.rs holds the 1 interface and the NotSupported value, and mac.rs, linux.rs and windows.rs implement it (design A19, understand N13). It depends on no crate of the workspace, no context owns it, and each context calls it directly (decompose N7, strategize N1). Only these files hold OS cfg in production code (PL-2).
codeA8highThe implementation plan follows the 9 phases of the design migration plan in order: Phase 0, Phase P, then Phases 1 to 7 (design A19, A22, understand N19). Slice numbers follow the phases, and the Phase P slice comes right after the Phase 0 slice, so a slice is released only when its gate passes (design D9).
codeA9mediumThe fitness tests extend crates/horch-core/tests/arch_scan.rs, which already scans source files for forbidden lines. No new tool is needed.
codeA10mediumCoined terms Verified Verdict, Stall Rung, Judged Tree, Path Claim, Awake Instant and Judge Finding name value objects and an entity that the canvases describe but do not name.
codeA11highworker-profiles owns the fleet-run wrapper and the command start-agent-process (decision D3 option B, connect N5). The wrapper builds the private config home, scrubs the environment, maps CLI events, writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, and calls the platform interface for the process group and kill. Its composition root stays crates/horch/src/cmd/fleet_run.rs.
codeA12highideas takes the pattern domain-model, the most demanding pattern of its subdomain (strategize D1 option C). Only the plan validation module has an aggregate, Plan. Idea intake and questions stay active-record records in IdeasStore.
codeA13mediumintegration asks worktree-custody for each rescue ref through an in-process call (port RescueRefGateway), because worktree-custody alone writes refs under refs/horch/rescue/ (define N5, N6). No new cross-process message exists for it.
codeA14highThe 1 needs-you list belongs to ideas (decompose N9). task-execution publishes task-escalated and writes no needs-you file; ideas puts the task on the list beside approvals and escalated questions.
codeA15mediumThe Phase 0 list of expected failures is a file in the repository that the test runner reads. Each entry names a test and the phase that makes it green. The design does not name the path, so the plan names none.
contractsA1highAnswers connect N1 and code N1: contracts cover only the messages that leave the horch process or have a human, an agent or an external system on 1 end: the command channel, the file protocol and the external facts. The 21 in-process messages get no wire schema; contracts.md lists them for code-level tests.
contractsA2highAnswers code N2: every entry id equals its connect message id, so the code.json tests 'contract: <id>' and 'idempotent: <id>' bind to these entries. Each semantics line keeps the connect idempotency key as written.
contractsA3highEvery entry uses the snake_case field names of the design (decision D1, option B). write-result, submit-plan, assign-task and heartbeat-written copy the field names of the design examples of result.json, plan.yaml, task.yaml and heartbeat.json; the other entries use the connect payload names, which connect now writes in snake_case.
contractsA4highInterim retired: decision D1 is decided (option B), so no entry keeps a camelCase field name. Each former camelCase name has its snake_case form (ideaId is idea_id, taskId is task_id, prUrl is pr_url).
contractsA5highId formats come from the comments of the design ledger schema: I-0007, F-0003, T-0007-02, T-0007-02/A1 or I-0007/clarifying/1, T-0007-02/A1/Q1, refs/horch/rescue/T-0007-03/1, fleet/I-0007/T-0007-03.
contractsA6mediumA Markdown file of the file protocol (assumptions.md, spec.md) is carried as 1 string field with the whole file content; requirements.yaml and plan.yaml are carried as objects with the design field names.
contractsA7mediumanswer-question carries the answer as an object {case, text}. case is the closed list of ledger questions.answer_case (covered, revise, replan, own_decision). connect writes 'answer|assumption'; an own_decision answer is the assumption case.
contractsA8mediumreplan-task carries planChange as 1 task in the plan.yaml task shape, with the same key.
contractsA9mediumresult.json requires task, attempt, status, summary and commits; files_changed, acceptance_self_check and notes_for_next are optional. commits may be empty.
contractsA10mediumattempt-exited exitStatus is the integer exit code, or null when a signal ended the process (ledger attempts.exit_code is nullable).
contractsA11highEach command channel reply carries outcome (accepted or refused). A refused reply carries reason; an accepted reply carries the ids it creates and no reason. approve-assumptions replies outcome and reason only; the boolean approved is retired (orchestrator, D15).
contractsA12mediumThe request of trial-merge-result names the other side as a feature id or the literal 'primary' for the primary branch.
contractsA13hightask.kind and task-escalated.reason stay open strings: the design names known values but no closed list.
contractsA14mediumidempotency_key is an opaque string of 1 to 128 characters that the horch CLI makes once per command run. The design and connect give no format, so the schema fixes only its type and length.
contractsA15highheartbeat-written and attempt-exited have a contract although organise puts the wrapper and task-execution in 1 deployable: the fleet-run wrapper is its own process and writes heartbeat.json and exit.json, so each file crosses a process boundary (revision context, contracts; consistency gap 5). The check warns about both; the warnings are expected.
contractsA16mediumtask-verdict-written decision is the closed list done or ready, from the Verifier row of the design (it moves the task to done or back to ready). connect names the field decision but gives no list.
contractsA17mediumstart-work carries START.md as 3 fields (task_yaml, rescue_commit, progress_notes) from connect; fleetd renders them as Markdown. A retry has both rescue_commit and progress_notes (design: Reuse, don't redo).
